title.zh: 卷三百一十 列傳第六十九 李迪 王曾 張知白 杜衍
title.en: Volume 310 Biographies 69: Li Di, Wang Ceng, Zhang Zhibai, Du Yan
title.raw: 卷三百一十 列傳第六十九 李迪 王曾 張知白 杜衍 Volume 310 Biographies 69: Li Di, Wang Ceng, Zhang Zhibai, Du Yan

sentences.zh: 李迪，字復古，其先趙郡人，後徙幽州。

translations.literal: Li Di, style name Fugu, his ancestors were people of Zhao Commandery, and later moved to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Di, whose style name was Fugu, came from Zhao Commandery by ancestry; his family later relocated to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖在欽，避五代亂，又徙家濮。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zaiqin, avoiding the chaos of the Five Dynasties, again moved the family to Pu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zaiqin fled the turmoil of the Five Dynasties period and resettled the family in Pu.

sentences.zh: 迪深厚有器局，嘗攜其所為文見柳開，開奇之曰：「公輔材也。」

translations.literal: Di was deep and weighty in bearing and had great capacity. Once he brought his own writings to see Liu Kai. Kai marveled at him and said, "Material for grand councilor."
translations.idiomatic: Di was grave and far-sighted. He once presented his writings to Liu Kai, who was struck by them and declared, "Here is a man fit to serve as chief minister."

sentences.zh: 舉進士第一，授將作監丞，歷通判徐、兗州。

translations.literal: He placed first in the jinshi examination, was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, and successively served as vice-prefect of Xu and Yan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Having topped the jinshi rolls, he was made Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and later served as vice-prefect of Xu and Yan.

sentences.zh: 改秘書省著作郎、直史館，為三司鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Compiler in the Secretariat and Drafter in the Historiography Institute, and served as Salt and Iron Commissioner of the Three Bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as a compiler in the Secretariat and drafter in the Historiography Institute, and appointed Salt and Iron Commissioner of the Three Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 東封泰山，復通判兗州，坐嘗解開封府進士失當，謫監海州稅。

translations.literal: When the emperor performed the Fengshan rites at Mount Tai, he again served as vice-prefect of Yan. Because he had once improperly released jinshi candidates of the Kaifeng prefectural examination, he was demoted to supervise maritime tax at Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the eastern Fengshan pilgrimage he again served as vice-prefect of Yan, but was demoted to oversee Haizhou's maritime tax after improperly releasing candidates in a Kaifeng prefectural examination.

sentences.zh: 改右司諫，起知鄆州，詔糾察在京刑獄，遷起居舍人，安撫江、淮，以尚書吏部員外郎為三司鹽鐵副使，擢知制誥。

translations.literal: He was made Right Remonstrance Official, then appointed prefect of Yanzhou. He was ordered to investigate capital criminal cases, promoted to Attendant of Daily Affairs, pacified Jiang and Huai, served as Vice Commissioner of Salt and Iron of the Three Bureaus with the rank of Vice Minister of Personnel in the Ministry of Personnel, and was elevated to Drafter of Imperial Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Right Remonstrance Official and then prefect of Yanzhou, he was charged with inspecting capital prisons, made Attendant of Daily Affairs, and sent to pacify the Jiang-Huai region. As Vice Minister of Personnel he became Vice Commissioner of Salt and Iron and was raised to Drafter of Imperial Edicts.

sentences.zh: 真宗幸亳，為留守判官，遂知亳州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong visited Bo, Di served as administrative aide to the regent and then became prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong toured Bo, Di served as the regent's administrative aide and was subsequently appointed prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 亡卒群剽城邑，發兵捕之，久不得。

translations.literal: Deserters banded together to plunder cities and towns. Troops were sent to capture them but for a long time they could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Bands of deserters were raiding towns, and though troops were dispatched to hunt them down, the pursuit dragged on without success.

sentences.zh: 迪至，悉罷所發兵，陰聽察知賊區處，部勒驍銳士，擒賊，斬以徇。

translations.literal: When Di arrived, he dismissed all the troops that had been sent out, secretly investigated to learn where the bandits were, deployed crack troops, captured the bandits, and executed them as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: On arriving, Di disbanded the troops already in the field, quietly traced the bandits' haunts, led picked fighters against them, seized the ringleaders, and had them beheaded as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 代歸，會唃廝囉叛，帝憂關中，召對長春殿，進右諫議大夫、集賢院學士、知永興軍。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned, Gusiluo rebelled. The emperor worried about Guanzhong, summoned him for audience at the Changchun Hall, and promoted him to Right Remonstrance Grandee, Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and military commissioner of Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: After his tour of duty he was recalled just as Gusiluo rose in revolt. Anxious about Guanzhong, the emperor summoned him to the Changchun Hall and made him Right Remonstrance Grandee, an academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and military commissioner of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 城中多無賴子弟，喜犯法，迪奏取其甚者，部送闕下。

translations.literal: In the city there were many unruly young men who delighted in breaking the law. Di memorialized to take the worst offenders and escort them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The city teemed with lawless youths, and Di had the worst of them arrested and sent under guard to the capital.

sentences.zh: 徙陝西都轉運使，入為翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Director-General of Transport for Shaanxi and entered the capital as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to head transport in Shaanxi, then recalled to the capital as a Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 嘗歸沐，忽傳詔對內東門，出三司使馬元方所上歲出入材用數以示迪。

translations.literal: Once when he had returned home on leave, he was suddenly summoned by edict to the Inner Eastern Gate. The emperor produced the annual revenue and expenditure figures submitted by Three Bureaus Commissioner Ma Yuanfang and showed them to Di.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while home on leave, he was abruptly summoned to the Inner Eastern Gate, where the emperor showed him the annual revenue and expenditure report that Ma Yuanfang of the Three Bureaus had submitted.

sentences.zh: 時頻歲蝗旱，問何以濟，迪請發內藏庫以佐國用，則賦斂寬，民不勞矣。

translations.literal: Locusts and drought had struck year after year. The emperor asked how to relieve the distress. Di requested that the inner treasury be opened to supplement state finances, so that levies could be eased and the people would not be overburdened.
translations.idiomatic: After years of locusts and drought the emperor asked how to ease the crisis. Di urged drawing on the inner treasury to shore up state finances so that taxes could be lightened and the people spared further hardship.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕欲用李士衡代元方，俟其至，當出金帛數百萬借三司。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I intend to use Li Shiheng to replace Yuanfang. When he arrives, I shall release several million in gold and silk to lend to the Three Bureaus."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I plan to replace Yuanfang with Li Shiheng. When he arrives I will release several million in gold and silk to lend the Three Bureaus."

sentences.zh: 」迪曰：「天子於財無內外，願下詔賜三司，以示恩德，何必曰借。

translations.literal: Di said, "For the Son of Heaven there is no inner or outer in matters of wealth. I hope Your Majesty will issue an edict granting funds to the Three Bureaus to display imperial grace—why must it be called a loan?"
translations.idiomatic: Di replied, "The sovereign's wealth knows no inner or outer court. Grant the funds by edict as a mark of grace—why call it a loan?"

sentences.zh: 」帝悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 又言：「陛下東封時，敕所過毋伐木除道，即驛舍或州治為行宮，裁令加塗塈而已。

translations.literal: He also said, "When Your Majesty performed the eastern Fengshan rites, you ordered that along the route no trees be felled nor roads cleared; post stations or prefectural seats were made into temporary palaces with only whitewashing added.
translations.idiomatic: He went on, "On the eastern Fengshan tour Your Majesty forbade felling trees or clearing roads along the route; post stations and prefectural seats served as temporary palaces with no more than a coat of whitewash.

sentences.zh: 及幸汾、亳，土木之役，過往時幾百倍。

translations.literal: When you visited Fen and Bo, the construction work was nearly a hundred times greater than before."
translations.idiomatic: Yet on the tours to Fen and Bo, construction costs ran nearly a hundred times higher."

sentences.zh: 今蝗旱之災，殆天意所以儆陛下也。

translations.literal: The present disasters of locusts and drought are perhaps Heaven's way of warning Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Surely the locusts and drought are Heaven's warning to Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」帝深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply persuaded.

sentences.zh: 他日，又召對龍圖閣，命迪草詔，徐謂迪曰：「曹瑋在秦州，屢請益兵，未及遣，遽辭州事，第怯耳。

translations.literal: Another day he was again summoned to the Dragon Diagram Hall, ordered to draft an edict, and the emperor said slowly to Di, "Cao Wei is at Qinzhou. He has repeatedly requested more troops. Before they could be sent, he suddenly resigned his prefectural post—he is simply timid.
translations.idiomatic: On another day Di was summoned to the Dragon Diagram Hall to draft an edict. The emperor said slowly, "Cao Wei at Qinzhou has repeatedly asked for reinforcements. Before any could be sent he abruptly resigned his post—he is simply afraid.

sentences.zh: 誰可代瑋者？

translations.literal: Who can replace Wei?"
translations.idiomatic: Who can replace him?"

sentences.zh: 」迪對曰：「瑋知唃廝囉欲入寇，且窺關中，故請益兵為備，非怯也。

translations.literal: Di replied, "Wei knows that Gusiluo intends to invade and is also watching Guanzhong, so he requested more troops as a precaution—it is not timidity.
translations.idiomatic: Di answered, "Wei knows Gusiluo means to raid and is eyeing Guanzhong, so he sought more troops as a precaution—that is not cowardice.

sentences.zh: 且瑋有謀略，諸將皆非其比，何可代？

translations.literal: Moreover Wei has strategy; none of the generals can compare with him—how can he be replaced?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, none of the generals match his strategic gifts—who could replace him?

sentences.zh: 陛下重發兵，豈非將上玉皇聖號，惡兵出宜秋門邪？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty sends out troops again in force, is it not because you are about to assume the sacred title of Jade Emperor and dislike troops marching out the Yiqiu Gate?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty is reluctant to dispatch more troops, is it not because you are about to assume the Jade Emperor's sacred title and wish to avoid armies marching out the Yiqiu Gate?

sentences.zh: 今關右兵多，可分兵赴瑋。

translations.literal: Now there are many troops in the Guanxi region; troops can be divided and sent to Wei."
translations.idiomatic: There are ample troops in the west—detach a portion for Wei."

sentences.zh: 」帝因問關右兵幾何，對曰：「臣向在陝西，以方寸小冊書兵糧數備調發，今猶置佩囊中。

translations.literal: The emperor then asked how many troops were in Guanxi. He replied, "When I was in Shaanxi I recorded troop and grain figures in a small booklet for ready dispatch, and I still carry it in my belt pouch."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked how many troops stood in the west. Di said, "When I served in Shaanxi I kept troop and grain tallies in a pocket notebook for ready reference, and I still carry it."

sentences.zh: 」帝令自探取，目黃門取紙筆，具疏某處當留兵若干，餘悉赴塞下。

translations.literal: The emperor told him to take it out himself, signaled the Yellow Gate attendants for paper and brush, and Di set forth in detail how many troops should remain at each place, with the rest all sent to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bade him produce it, had attendants bring paper and brush, and Di listed how many men to leave at each post and sent the rest to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 帝顧曰：「真所謂頗、牧在禁中矣。

translations.literal: The emperor looked back and said, "Truly this is what they mean by having Lian Po and Li Mu within the palace."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exclaimed, "Truly we have our Lian Po and Li Mu right here in the palace."

sentences.zh: 」未久，唃廝囉果犯邊。

translations.literal: Before long Gusiluo did invade the border.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gusiluo did raid the frontier.

sentences.zh: 秦州方出兵，復召迪問曰：「瑋此舉勝乎？

translations.literal: Qinzhou had just sent out troops when Di was summoned again and asked, "Will Wei win this engagement?"
translations.idiomatic: Just as Qinzhou's troops marched out, Di was summoned again. "Will Wei prevail?" the emperor asked.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「必勝。

translations.literal: He replied, "He will certainly win."
translations.idiomatic: "He will win," Di replied.

sentences.zh: 」居數日，奏至，瑋與敵戰三都谷，果大勝。

translations.literal: After several days a report arrived: Wei had fought the enemy at Sandu Valley and indeed won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the report came: Wei had routed the enemy at Sandu Valley.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿何以知瑋必勝？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "How did you know Wei would certainly win?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "How did you know he would win?"

sentences.zh: 」迪曰：「唃廝囉兵遠來，使諜者聲言以某日下秦州會食，以激怒瑋。

translations.literal: Di said, "Gusiluo's troops had come from afar. He sent spies to proclaim that on a certain day they would descend on Qinzhou to feast, intending to provoke Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Di said, "Gusiluo's men had marched far. His spies spread word that on a set day they would descend on Qinzhou to feast, hoping to goad Wei into rash action.

sentences.zh: 瑋勒兵不動，坐待敵至，是以逸待勞也。

translations.literal: Wei held his troops motionless and sat waiting for the enemy to arrive—thus meeting fatigue with rested strength.
translations.idiomatic: Wei held his army still and waited for them to come—meeting their fatigue with his rested troops.

sentences.zh: 臣用此知其勝。

translations.literal: From this your servant knew he would win."
translations.idiomatic: That is how I knew he would prevail."

sentences.zh: 」帝益重之，自是欲大用矣。

translations.literal: The emperor valued him all the more, and from then on intended to employ him in great matters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor esteemed him still more and from then on meant to give him major responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 初，上將立章獻后，迪屢上疏諫，以章獻起於寒微，不可母天下。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was about to install Empress Zhangxian, Di repeatedly memorialized in remonstrance, holding that Zhangxian had risen from humble origins and could not be mother to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was preparing to elevate Empress Zhangxian, Di repeatedly remonstrated, arguing that a woman of such humble birth could not be empress mother of the realm.

sentences.zh: 章獻深銜之。

translations.literal: Zhangxian bore a deep grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangxian never forgave him.

sentences.zh: 天禧中，拜給事中、參知政事。

translations.literal: In the Tianxi era he was appointed Attendant Gentleman and Participant in Deliberations on Government Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianxi reign he was made Attendant Gentleman and Participant in Deliberations on Government Affairs.

sentences.zh: 周懷政之誅，帝怒甚，欲責及太子，群臣莫敢言。

translations.literal: When Zhou Huaizheng was executed, the emperor was extremely angry and wished to extend blame to the crown prince. None of the ministers dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou Huaizheng's execution the emperor was furious and inclined to implicate the crown prince, but none of the ministers dared speak up.

sentences.zh: 迪從容奏曰：「陛下有幾子？

translations.literal: Di calmly submitted, "How many sons does Your Majesty have?
translations.idiomatic: Di said calmly, "How many sons does Your Majesty have?

sentences.zh: 乃欲為此計。

translations.literal: Yet you wish to carry out this plan."
translations.idiomatic: —and yet you would contemplate such a course?"

sentences.zh: 」上大寤，由是獨誅懷政等。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly came to his senses, and therefore only Huaizheng and his associates were executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to his senses and punished only Huaizheng and his circle.

sentences.zh: 仁宗為皇太子，除太子太傅，迪辭以太宗時未嘗立保傅，止兼太子賓客，詔皇太子禮賓客如師傅。

translations.literal: When Renzong was crown prince, Di was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent. Di declined on the ground that in Taizong's time no guardian or tutor had been appointed, and accepted only the concurrent post of Guest of the Heir Apparent. An edict ordered the crown prince to treat the Guest with the ceremony due a tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong was crown prince, Di was named Grand Preceptor but declined, noting that Taizong had never appointed guardian-tutors, and accepted only the concurrent post of Guest of the Heir Apparent. An edict directed the prince to honor his Guest as he would a tutor.

sentences.zh: 加禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was further made Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 寇準罷，帝欲相迪，迪固辭。

translations.literal: When Kou Zhun was dismissed, the emperor wished to make Di chief minister, but Di firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: After Kou Zhun's dismissal the emperor wished to make Di chief minister, but Di firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 一日，對滋福殿，有頃，皇太子出拜曰：「陛下用賓客為宰相，敢以謝。

translations.literal: One day, while in audience at the Zifu Hall, after a while the crown prince came out, bowed, and said, "Your Majesty has made your Guest chief minister—I venture to offer thanks."
translations.idiomatic: One day at an audience in the Zifu Hall the crown prince appeared, bowed, and said, "Your Majesty has elevated my Guest to chief minister—I thank you on his behalf."

sentences.zh: 」帝顧謂迪曰：「尚可辭邪！

translations.literal: The emperor turned to Di and said, "Can you still decline!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Di and said, "Can you still refuse?"

sentences.zh: 」拜吏部侍郎兼太子少傅、同中書門下平章事、景靈宮使、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, concurrent Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Grand Councilor with the Tong Zhongshu Menxia Pingzhangshi title, Commissioner of the Jingling Palace, and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Di was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Grand Councilor, Commissioner of the Jingling Palace, and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 初，真宗不豫，寇準議皇太子總軍國事，迪贊其策，丁謂以為不便，曰：「即日上體平，朝廷何以處此？

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhenzong fell ill, Kou Zhun proposed that the crown prince assume overall charge of military and civil affairs. Di endorsed the plan. Ding Wei thought it inconvenient and said, "If His Majesty's health is restored tomorrow, how will the court deal with this arrangement?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong fell ill, Kou Zhun proposed putting the crown prince in charge of state and military affairs. Di backed the plan, but Ding Wei objected: "If the emperor recovers tomorrow, how will the court undo this?"

sentences.zh: 」迪曰：「太子監國，非古制邪？

translations.literal: Di said, "The crown prince overseeing the state—is that not an ancient institution?"
translations.idiomatic: Di replied, "A crown prince overseeing the realm—is that not ancient precedent?"

sentences.zh: 」力爭不已。

translations.literal: He argued forcefully without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the point relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 於是皇太子於資善堂聽常事，他皆聽旨。

translations.literal: Thereupon the crown prince heard routine business at the Hall of Cultivating Goodness, while all else awaited imperial instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince thereafter heard routine business in the Hall of Cultivating Goodness; everything else awaited the emperor's word.

sentences.zh: 準既貶，謂寖擅權用事，至除吏不以聞。

translations.literal: After Zhun was demoted, Wei gradually usurped power and conducted affairs, even appointing officials without reporting to the court.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhun's fall, Ding Wei gradually monopolized power, even appointing officials without informing the court.

sentences.zh: 迪憤然語同列曰：「迪起布衣至宰相，有以報國，死猶不恨，安能附權幸為自安計邪！

translations.literal: Di said angrily to his colleagues, "Di rose from commoner to chief minister with means to repay the state. I would not regret death—how could I cling to the powerful for my own security!"
translations.idiomatic: Di said angrily to his colleagues, "I rose from commoner to chief minister to serve the state. I would die without regret—how could I cling to the powerful for my own safety?"

sentences.zh: 」自此不協。

translations.literal: From then on they were at odds.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they were at odds.

sentences.zh: 時議二府皆進秩兼東宮官，迪以為不可。

translations.literal: At the time it was proposed that both chief councils advance in rank and concurrently hold Eastern Palace offices. Di held this improper.
translations.idiomatic: A proposal then circulated to promote both chief councils and give them Eastern Palace posts. Di opposed it.

sentences.zh: 謂又欲引林特為樞密副使，而遷迪中書侍郎兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Wei also wished to bring in Lin Te as Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, while transferring Di to Vice Director of the Secretariat with concurrent Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei also sought to install Lin Te as Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs while moving Di to Vice Director of the Secretariat with concurrent Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 故事，宰相無為左丞者。

translations.literal: By precedent no chief minister had ever held the post of Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent no chief minister had ever served as Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 既而帝御長春殿，內出制書置榻前，謂輔臣曰：「此卿等兼東宮官制書也。

translations.literal: Soon the emperor held court at the Changchun Hall, produced appointment documents from within, placed them before the couch, and said to the chief ministers, "These are your appointment documents for concurrent Eastern Palace offices."
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor held court at the Changchun Hall, laid out appointment documents, and told the chief ministers, "These appoint you to concurrent Eastern Palace offices."

sentences.zh: 」迪進曰：「東宮官屬不當增置，臣不敢受此命。

translations.literal: Di stepped forward and said, "Eastern Palace staff should not be increased. Your servant dares not accept this commission.
translations.idiomatic: Di stepped forward. "Eastern Palace staff should not be expanded, and I dare not accept this commission.

sentences.zh: 宰相丁謂罔上弄權，私林特、錢惟演而嫉寇準。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Ding Wei deceives the throne and manipulates power, favoring Lin Te and Qian Weiyan while hating Kou Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Ding Wei deceives the throne and abuses power, favoring Lin Te and Qian Weiyan while persecuting Kou Zhun.

sentences.zh: 特子殺人，事寢不治，準無罪罷斥，惟演姻家使預政，曹利用、馮拯相為朋黨。

translations.literal: Te's son committed murder but the case was buried without prosecution. Zhun was dismissed though guiltless. Weiyan, a relation by marriage, was allowed to participate in government. Cao Liyong and Feng Zheng act as a faction together.
translations.idiomatic: Te's son committed murder yet the case was buried. Zhun was banished though innocent. Weiyan, a relation by marriage, was allowed into government. Cao Liyong and Feng Zheng form a clique together.

sentences.zh: 臣願與謂俱罷，付御史臺劾正。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to be dismissed together with Wei and handed over to the Censorate for investigation and correction."
translations.idiomatic: I ask to be dismissed together with Wei and handed to the Censorate for investigation."

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，留制不下，左遷迪戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, withheld the documents without issuing them, and demoted Di to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, withheld the appointments, and demoted Di to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 謂再對，傳口詔入中書復視事，出迪知鄆州。

translations.literal: Wei had another audience, transmitted an oral edict for Di to return to the Secretariat and resume duties, and sent Di out as prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei gained another audience, had an oral edict read restoring Di to the Secretariat, then sent him out as prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，太后預政，貶準雷州，以迪朋黨傅會，貶衡州團練副使。

translations.literal: When Renzong ascended the throne the empress dowager participated in government. Zhun was demoted to Leizhou. Di was charged with factional collusion and demoted to Vice Military Training Commissioner of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong ascended the throne the empress dowager ruled from behind the screen. Zhun was banished to Leizhou; Di was accused of factional collusion and demoted to Vice Military Training Commissioner of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 謂使人迫之，或諷謂曰：「迪若貶死，公如士論何？

translations.literal: Wei sent men to press him hard. Someone subtly urged Wei, "If Di dies in exile, what will scholars say of you?"
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei sent men to hound him. Someone hinted, "If Di dies in exile, what will scholars say of you?"

sentences.zh: 」謂曰：「異日諸生記事，不過曰『天下惜之』而已。

translations.literal: Wei said, "When scholars of later days record events, they will only say 'the realm lamented him'—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei replied, "Future scholars will only write that the realm lamented him—that is all."

sentences.zh: 」謂敗，起為秘書監、知舒州，歷江寧府、兗州、青州，復兵部侍郎、知河南府。

translations.literal: When Wei fell, Di was recalled as Director of the Secretariat and prefect of Shuzhou, served successively at Jiangning, Yan, and Qing prefectures, and was again made Vice Minister of War and prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After Ding Wei's fall Di was recalled as Director of the Secretariat and prefect of Shuzhou, later served at Jiangning, Yan, and Qing, and was again made Vice Minister of War and prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 來朝京師，時太后垂簾，語迪曰：「卿向不欲吾預國事，殆過矣。

translations.literal: When he came to court at the capital, the empress dowager was behind the screen. She said to Di, "You once did not wish me to participate in state affairs—perhaps that went too far.
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to the capital, with the empress dowager still behind the screen, she told Di, "You once opposed my participation in government—perhaps you went too far.

sentences.zh: 今日吾保養天子至此，卿以為何如？

translations.literal: Today I have nurtured the Son of Heaven to this point—what do you think of that?"
translations.idiomatic: Today I have raised the Son of Heaven to this point—what do you think of that?"

sentences.zh: 」迪對曰：「臣受先帝厚恩，今日見天子明聖，臣不知皇太后盛德，乃至於此。

translations.literal: Di replied, "Your servant received deep favor from the late emperor. Today I see the Son of Heaven bright and sagely. Your servant did not know the empress dowager's great virtue extended to this."
translations.idiomatic: Di answered, "I owed deep gratitude to the late emperor. Today I see a bright and sagely sovereign—I did not know the empress dowager's virtue extended so far."

sentences.zh: 」太后亦喜。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was also pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was pleased as well.

sentences.zh: 以尚書左丞知河陽，遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: As Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs he was made military commissioner of Heyang, then promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: As Left Vice Director he was made military commissioner of Heyang, then promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 太后崩，召為資政殿學士、判尚書都省。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died, he was summoned as Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and given charge of the overall Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager's death he was summoned as Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance with charge of the overall Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復拜同中書門下平章事、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed Grand Councilor with the Tong Zhongshu Menxia Pingzhangshi title and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again appointed Grand Councilor and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 景祐中，范諷得罪，迪坐姻黨，罷為刑部尚書，知亳州，改相州。

translations.literal: In the Jingyou era Fan Feng offended and was punished. Di was implicated as a relation by marriage and dismissed to Minister of Justice, prefect of Bozhou, then transferred to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyou era Fan Feng fell afoul of the court. Di was implicated through marriage ties, dismissed to Minister of Justice and prefect of Bozhou, then transferred to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 既而為資政殿大學士、翰林侍讀學士，留京師。

translations.literal: He was then made Grand Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and Hanlin Attendant Reader, remaining at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Grand Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and Hanlin Attendant Reader and kept at the capital.

sentences.zh: 迪素惡呂夷簡，因奏夷簡私交荊王元儼，嘗為補門下僧惠清為守闕鑒義。

translations.literal: Di had long disliked Lü Yijian and memorialized that Yijian had private dealings with Prince Jing, Yuan Yan, and had once arranged for the monk Huiqing of the Gate of the Heir Apparent to be appointed as Awaiting-Appointment Regulator of Credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Di had long disliked Lü Yijian and accused him of private dealings with Prince Jing Yuan Yan, including once securing an appointment for the monk Huiqing as Awaiting-Appointment Regulator of Credentials.

sentences.zh: 夷簡請辨，詔訊之，乃迪在中書所行事，夷簡以齋祠不預。

translations.literal: Yijian requested investigation. An edict ordered inquiry, and it turned out to have been Di's own act while in the Secretariat; Yijian had been absent for fasting and sacrifice rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian demanded an inquiry. The investigation showed the act had been Di's own doing while in the Secretariat; Yijian had been absent for ritual fasting.

sentences.zh: 降太常卿、知密州。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 復刑部尚書、知徐州。

translations.literal: He was again made Minister of Justice and prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as Minister of Justice and prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 迪奏所部鄰兗州，欲行縣因祠嶽為上祈年、禱皇子。

translations.literal: Di memorialized that his jurisdiction bordered Yanzhou and that he wished to tour the counties and, taking advantage of sacrifices at the sacred mountain, pray for a good harvest and for a royal son on the emperor's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Di noted that his jurisdiction bordered Yanzhou and asked to tour the counties, offering prayers at the sacred mountain for a good harvest and a royal heir on the emperor's behalf.

sentences.zh: 仁宗語輔臣曰：「大臣當為百姓訪疾苦，祈禱非迪所宜，其毋令往。

translations.literal: Renzong told the chief ministers, "Great ministers should inquire into the people's hardships. Prayer rites are not what Di should do—do not let him go."
translations.idiomatic: Renzong told his ministers, "Great ministers should investigate the people's hardships. Prayer rites are not Di's proper role—do not let him go."

sentences.zh: 」久之，改戶部尚書、知兗州，復拜資政殿大學士。

translations.literal: After a long while he was changed to Minister of Revenue and prefect of Yanzhou, and again appointed Grand Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was made Minister of Revenue and prefect of Yanzhou, and again appointed Grand Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance.

sentences.zh: 元昊攻延州，武事久弛，守將或為他名以避兵。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao attacked Yanzhou. Military affairs had long been neglected, and some frontier commanders took other names to avoid military duty.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao attacked Yanzhou, military readiness had long lapsed, and some frontier commanders even assumed other names to evade service.

sentences.zh: 迪願守邊，詔不許，然甚壯其意。

translations.literal: Di volunteered to guard the frontier. An edict did not permit it, yet the emperor greatly admired his spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Di volunteered for frontier duty. The court refused, but the emperor greatly admired his spirit.

sentences.zh: 除彰信軍節度使、知天雄軍，徙青州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Commissioner of the Zhangxin Army and given charge of the Tianxiong Army, then transferred to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Military Commissioner of the Zhangxin Army with charge of Tianxiong, then transferred to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 逾年，之本鎮。

translations.literal: After more than a year he returned to his original command.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he returned to his original command.

sentences.zh: 請老，以太子太傅致仕，歸濮州。

translations.literal: He requested retirement on account of age, retired as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and returned to Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement, left office as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and returned to Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 後其子柬之為侍御史知雜事，奉迪來京師。

translations.literal: Later his son Jianzhi served as Attendant Censor with charge of miscellaneous affairs and brought Di to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later his son Jianzhi, serving as Attendant Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs, brought him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝數遣使問勞，欲召見，以疾辭。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly sent envoys to inquire after his health and wished to summon him for audience, but he declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly sent envoys to inquire after him and wished to summon him, but he declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 薨，年七十七。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈司空、侍中，諡文定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the titles of Minister of Works and Palace Attendant, with the posthumous name Wending.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Works and Palace Attendant, with the posthumous name Wending.

sentences.zh: 帝篆其墓碑曰「遺直之碑」，又改所葬鄧侯鄉曰遺直鄉。

translations.literal: The emperor inscribed his tomb stele "Stele of the Upright Legacy," and also changed the name of the Deng Marquis township where he was buried to the Township of the Upright Legacy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inscribed his tomb stele "Stele of the Upright Legacy" and renamed the Deng Marquis township where he was buried the Township of the Upright Legacy.

sentences.zh: 子：柬之、肅之、承之、及之。

translations.literal: Sons: Jianzhi, Suzhi, Chengzhi, and Jizhi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Jianzhi, Suzhi, Chengzhi, and Jizhi.

sentences.zh: 孫：孝壽、孝基、孝稱。

translations.literal: Grandsons: Xiaoshou, Xiaoji, and Xiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandsons were Xiaoshou, Xiaoji, and Xiaocheng.

sentences.zh: 子 柬之

translations.literal: Son: Jianzhi
translations.idiomatic: Son: Jianzhi

sentences.zh: 柬之，字公明，曉國朝典故。

translations.literal: Jianzhi, style name Gongming, was versed in the precedents and institutions of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi, whose style name was Gongming, was thoroughly versed in the precedents of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 獻文，召試，賜進士出身，為館閣校勘、宣化軍使。

translations.literal: He presented writings, was summoned for examination, granted jinshi status, and served as collator in the Hall of Literature and commissioner of the Xuanhua Army.
translations.idiomatic: After presenting his writings and passing a palace examination, he was granted jinshi status and appointed collator in the Hall of Literature and commissioner of the Xuanhua Army.

sentences.zh: 境上有廢河故道，官收行者稅，謂之「乾渡錢」，奏除之。

translations.literal: Within his jurisdiction was an old course of a ruined river. The government collected a tax on travelers, called the "Dry Crossing Fee." He memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: An abandoned riverbed crossed his jurisdiction, and officials levied a "Dry Crossing Fee" on travelers. He memorialized to abolish the tax.

sentences.zh: 進直集賢院、判吏部南曹、開封府推官、鹽鐵判官，歷知邢、漢、廬州、鳳翔府，京東、陝西轉運使，擢侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: He advanced to drafter in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, served as judge of the Southern Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, investigating censor of Kaifeng, and Salt and Iron Commissioner, successively governed Xing, Han, Lu prefectures and Fengxiang, served as transport commissioner for Jingdong and Shaanxi, and was elevated to Attendant Censor with charge of miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to drafter in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, held posts in the Ministry of Personnel, Kaifeng, and the Salt and Iron Commission, governed several prefectures, headed transport in Jingdong and Shaanxi, and was elevated to Attendant Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs.

sentences.zh: 柬之自少受知於寇準，至是論準保護之功。

translations.literal: Jianzhi had from youth received Kou Zhun's favor. At this time he discussed Zhun's merit in protecting the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi had known Kou Zhun since youth and now spoke of Zhun's service in protecting the throne.

sentences.zh: 仁宗惻然，即賜其碑曰「旌忠」。

translations.literal: Renzong was moved and at once bestowed on him a stele inscribed "Commemorating Loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Renzong immediately granted him a stele inscribed "Commemorating Loyalty."

sentences.zh: 拜天章閣待制、河北都轉運使，加龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant Drafter of the Tianzhang Pavilion and Director-General of Transport for Hebei, and given the additional title of Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Attendant Drafter of the Tianzhang Pavilion and Director-General of Transport for Hebei, with the additional title of Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 建言補蔭之門太廣，遂詔裁定，自二府而下，通三歲減入仕者一千人。

translations.literal: He proposed that the avenues of hereditary privilege were too broad. An edict was issued to set limits, and from the two chief councils downward, over three years a thousand fewer persons entered office.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that hereditary privilege had grown too broad. The court issued limits, and within three years a thousand fewer people entered office from the chief councils down.

sentences.zh: 知荊南、河陽、澶州，改集賢院學士，判西京留司御史臺。

translations.literal: He governed Jingnan, Heyang, and Chan prefectures, was changed to Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and given charge of the Western Capital branch of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Jingnan, Heyang, and Chan, became Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and took charge of the Western Capital Censorate.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，富弼薦其學行，復舊職，兼侍讀。

translations.literal: When Yingzong ascended the throne, Fu Bi recommended his learning and conduct. He was restored to his former post and made concurrent Attendant Reader.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong ascended the throne, Fu Bi recommended his scholarship and character. He was restored to office and made Attendant Reader.

sentences.zh: 帝勞之曰：「卿通議耆儒，方諮訪以輔不逮，豈止經術而已。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted him, saying, "You are a veteran elder of broad counsel. I am consulting you to remedy my shortcomings—not for classical learning alone."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "You are a seasoned elder of broad counsel. I seek your advice to remedy my shortcomings—not merely for classical learning."

sentences.zh: 」帝頗欲肅正宮省，柬之諫曰：「陛下，長君也，立自宗藩，眾方觀望，願曲為容覆。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to discipline the palace and inner offices. Jianzhi remonstrated, "Your Majesty is the elder sovereign, raised from a collateral princely house. The realm is watching—please be lenient and accommodating."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to tighten discipline in the palace. Jianzhi urged, "Your Majesty is the elder sovereign, raised from a collateral house. The court is watching—please show forbearance."

sentences.zh: 」賜潁王生日禮物，故事，王拜賜竟，即退。

translations.literal: Birthday gifts were bestowed on Prince Ying of Ying. By precedent, after the prince bowed in thanks he withdrew at once.
translations.idiomatic: When birthday gifts were sent to Prince Ying, precedent required that he bow in thanks and withdraw at once.

sentences.zh: 帝諭王令留柬之食，冀其從容也。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed the prince to keep Jianzhi to dine, hoping he might speak at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the prince to keep Jianzhi for a meal, hoping for an unhurried conversation.

sentences.zh: 王即位未幾，柬之請老，自工部尚書拜太子少保致仕。

translations.literal: Not long after the prince ascended the throne, Jianzhi requested retirement and left office as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent from his post as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after the prince became emperor, Jianzhi requested retirement and left office as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, having served as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 舊無閣門謝辭式，特賜對延和，命之坐，仍置宴資善堂，遣使諭之曰：「以先帝梓宮在殯，朕不得為詩。

translations.literal: There had been no Gate protocol for farewell audiences. He was specially granted audience at the Yanhe Hall, ordered to sit, and a banquet was set in the Hall of Cultivating Goodness. An envoy was sent to tell him, "Because the late emperor's coffin is still in mourning, I cannot compose a poem myself."
translations.idiomatic: No Gate protocol existed for farewell audiences. He was granted a special audience in the Yanhe Hall, seated, and entertained at the Hall of Cultivating Goodness. An envoy explained, "With the late emperor's coffin still in mourning, I cannot compose a poem myself."

sentences.zh: 」令講讀官皆賦詩，勸勞甚渥，又敕王珪敘其事。

translations.literal: He ordered all lecture officials to compose poems. The encouragement and favors were very generous, and he also commanded Wang Gui to narrate the affair.
translations.idiomatic: He had the lecture officials compose poems instead. The honors were lavish, and he ordered Wang Gui to record the occasion.

sentences.zh: 柬之出都門，即幅巾白衣以見客。

translations.literal: Once Jianzhi passed the capital gate, he received guests in plain headcloth and white robes.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the capital gate he received guests in plain headcloth and white robes.

sentences.zh: 再遷少師。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 熙寧六年，卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xining he died at the age of seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Xining at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 有李受者，字益之，長沙之瀏陽人也。

translations.literal: There was one Li Shou, style name Yizhi, a native of Liuyang in Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Li Shou, style name Yizhi, a native of Liuyang in Changsha.

sentences.zh: 仕於治平中，至右諫議大夫、天章閣待制兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He served in the Zhiping era, rising to Right Remonstrance Grandee, Attendant Drafter of the Tianzhang Pavilion, and concurrent Attendant Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He served during the Zhiping era, rising to Right Remonstrance Grandee, Attendant Drafter of the Tianzhang Pavilion, and Attendant Reader.

sentences.zh: 屢以老乞骸骨，不聽。

translations.literal: He repeatedly begged to retire on account of age but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to retire on account of age, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，進給事中、龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended the throne, he was promoted to Attendant Gentleman and Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong ascended the throne, he was promoted to Attendant Gentleman and Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 復言：「臣在先帝時，年已七十，不敢竊祿以自安。

translations.literal: He again said, "Under the late emperor I was already seventy and dared not cling to salary for my own ease.
translations.idiomatic: He said again, "Under the late emperor I was already seventy and dared not cling to salary for comfort.

sentences.zh: 今又加數年，筋力憊矣，惟陛下哀之。

translations.literal: Now several more years have passed and my strength is spent—may Your Majesty show pity."
translations.idiomatic: Now several more years have passed and my strength is gone—may Your Majesty show pity."

sentences.zh: 」於是拜刑部侍郎致仕，賜宴賦詩及序，如柬之禮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice and retired, granted a banquet, poems, and a preface in the same manner as Jianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Vice Minister of Justice and retired with the same banquet, poems, and preface granted to Jianzhi.

sentences.zh: 相去數月，故時稱「二李」。

translations.literal: Only a few months separated them, so people at the time called them "the Two Lis."
translations.idiomatic: Their retirements were only months apart, so contemporaries called them "the Two Lis."

sentences.zh: 卒年八十，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at eighty and was posthumously given the title Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty and was posthumously honored as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 弟子 肅之

translations.literal: Nephew: Suzhi
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Suzhi

sentences.zh: 肅之，字公儀，迪弟子也。

translations.literal: Suzhi, style name Gongyi, was Di's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhi, whose style name was Gongyi, was Di's nephew.

sentences.zh: 以迪蔭，監大名府軍資庫。

translations.literal: Through Di's hereditary privilege he supervised the military supply depot of Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Through Di's hereditary privilege he supervised the military supply depot of Daming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大河溢，府檄修冠氏堤，工就弗擾，民悅之，請為宰。

translations.literal: The Yellow River overflowed. The prefecture ordered repairs to the Guanshi dike. The work was completed without disturbing the people, who were pleased and asked that he be made magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River overflowed, the prefecture ordered repairs to the Guanshi dike. He finished the work without troubling the people, who were so pleased they asked that he be made magistrate.

sentences.zh: 邑多盜，時出害人。

translations.literal: The district had many bandits who often came out to harm people.
translations.idiomatic: The district had many bandits who preyed on the people.

sentences.zh: 肅之令比戶置鼓，有盜，輒擊鼓，遠近皆應，盜為之衰止。

translations.literal: Suzhi ordered every household to keep a drum. When bandits appeared, drums were struck and neighbors near and far responded, so banditry declined and ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhi ordered every household to keep a drum. At the first sign of bandits, drums sounded and neighbors responded from near and far, and banditry dwindled away.

sentences.zh: 為御河催綱。

translations.literal: He served as transport escort commissioner on the Imperial Canal.
translations.idiomatic: He served as transport escort commissioner on the Imperial Canal.

sentences.zh: 橫隴之決，使者檄護金堤，滿歲無河患。

translations.literal: When the Henglong breach opened, an envoy ordered him to guard the Golden Dike. For a full year there was no river disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When the Henglong breach opened, he was ordered to guard the Golden Dike and kept the river in check for a full year.

sentences.zh: 通判澶州。

translations.literal: He served as vice-prefect of Chanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice-prefect of Chanzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹泛使將過郡，而樓堞壞圮，肅之謂郡守曰：「吾州為景德破敵之地，當示雄疆，今保障若是，且奈何？

translations.literal: Khitan envoys on a general mission were about to pass through the prefecture, but the towers and battlements were ruined. Suzhi said to the prefect, "Our prefecture is where Jingde defeated the enemy—we should display our strength. With our defenses in this state, what are we to do?"
translations.idiomatic: Khitan envoys were about to pass through, but the walls were in ruins. Suzhi told the prefect, "This is where Jingde defeated the Khitan—we must show strength. With our defenses like this, what will they think?"

sentences.zh: 」遂鳩工構城屋，凡千區。

translations.literal: He thereupon gathered workers and built a thousand sections of wall and towers.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered workers and rebuilt a thousand sections of wall and towers.

sentences.zh: 已而中貴人銜命來視，規置一新，驚賞嗟異，聞之朝。

translations.literal: Soon a palace eunuch came on imperial orders to inspect. Everything was newly laid out. He marveled and sighed in admiration and reported to court.
translations.idiomatic: When a palace eunuch came to inspect, he found everything restored and reported his amazement to court.

sentences.zh: 擢知德州，提點開封府界內縣鎮，夔路、湖南刑獄。

translations.literal: He was elevated to prefect of Dezhou, made intendant of counties and towns within the Kaifeng prefectural boundary, and given charge of criminal cases in Kuizhou circuit and Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Dezhou, made intendant of Kaifeng's subordinate counties and towns, and put in charge of criminal cases in Kuizhou and Hunan.

sentences.zh: 儂蠻暴嶺外，肅之親捍諸境，會蔣偕失利，亟率兵往躡於臨賀，賊引去。

translations.literal: The Nong tribes rioted beyond the ranges. Suzhi personally defended the borders. When Jiang Xie suffered defeat, he quickly led troops in pursuit to Linhe, and the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nong tribes rose beyond the ranges, Suzhi defended the borders in person. After Jiang Xie's defeat he swiftly pursued the rebels to Linhe and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 狄青、孫沔交薦之，徙湖北轉運使。

translations.literal: Di Qing and Sun Mian jointly recommended him, and he was transferred to transport commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Di Qing and Sun Mian jointly recommended him, and he was made transport commissioner of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 辰陽彭仕羲叛，討平之，猶以過左遷，知齊州。

translations.literal: Peng Shiyi of Chenyang rebelled. He suppressed the rebellion, yet was still demoted for faults and made prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed Peng Shiyi's rebellion in Chenyang but was still demoted for faults and made prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 改江東、兩浙、河北轉運使，進度支副使、江淮發運使。

translations.literal: He was changed to transport commissioner of Jiangdong, the two Zhe circuits, and Hebei, then promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Department of State Finance and transport dispatch commissioner for the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: He served as transport commissioner in Jiangdong, the two Zhe circuits, and Hebei, then became Vice Commissioner of the Department of State Finance and dispatch commissioner for the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 肅之內行修飭，母喪，廬墓三年，不入城郭。

translations.literal: Suzhi's private conduct was disciplined. When his mother died, he dwelt by her tomb for three years and did not enter towns or cities.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhi was disciplined in private life. After his mother's death he mourned at her tomb for three years without entering any town.

sentences.zh: 季弟承之，生而孤，鞠育誨道，至於成人，遂相繼為侍從。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chengzhi was orphaned at birth. He reared and instructed him until he came of age, and they successively became palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chengzhi was orphaned at birth; he raised and taught him to adulthood, and both eventually served at court.

sentences.zh: 帝稱其一門忠孝云。

translations.literal: The emperor praised their household for loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised their household for loyalty and filial piety.

sentences.zh: 弟子 承之

translations.literal: Nephew: Chengzhi
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Chengzhi

sentences.zh: 承之，字奉世，性嚴重，有忠節。

translations.literal: Chengzhi, style name Fengshi, was stern and weighty in character and possessed loyalty and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhi, whose style name was Fengshi, was grave in character and known for loyalty and integrity.

sentences.zh: 從兄柬之將仕以官，辭不受，而中進士第，調明州司法參軍。

translations.literal: His cousin Jianzhi was about to secure office for him, but he declined and instead passed the jinshi examination, being appointed judicial aide in Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Jianzhi offered him an official post, but he declined, passed the jinshi examination, and was appointed judicial aide in Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 郡守任情骫法，人莫敢忤，承之獨毅然力爭之。

translations.literal: The prefect acted arbitrarily and bent the law. No one dared oppose him, but Chengzhi alone stood firm and argued forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect bent the law at will, and no one dared oppose him—only Chengzhi stood firm and argued back.

sentences.zh: 守怒曰：「曹掾敢如是邪？

translations.literal: The prefect said angrily, "How dare a judicial aide act like this?"
translations.idiomatic: The prefect snapped, "How dare a judicial aide behave like this?"

sentences.zh: 」承之曰：「事始至，公自為之則已，既下有司，則當循三尺之法矣。

translations.literal: Chengzhi said, "When a matter first arises, if Your Excellency handles it yourself, that is one thing. Once it has been referred to the relevant office, the three-foot law must be followed."
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhi replied, "If Your Excellency handles a matter yourself, that is one thing. Once it is referred to the courts, the law must be followed."

sentences.zh: 」守憚其言。

translations.literal: The prefect feared his words.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect was silenced.

sentences.zh: 嘗建免役議，王安石見而稱之。

translations.literal: He once drafted a proposal on the exemption-from-corvée system. Wang Anshi saw it and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: He once drafted a proposal on corvée exemption, which Wang Anshi praised.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，以為條例司檢詳文字，得召見。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining he was made textual reviewer in the Regulations Office and summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xining reforms he was made textual reviewer in the Regulations Office and summoned to audience.

sentences.zh: 神宗語執政曰：「承之言制置司事甚詳，非他人所及也。

translations.literal: Shenzong told the chief ministers, "Chengzhi speaks on fiscal commission affairs in great detail—others cannot match him."
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong told the chief ministers, "Chengzhi's grasp of fiscal affairs is unrivaled."

sentences.zh: 」改京官。

translations.literal: He was changed to capital official rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to capital official rank.

sentences.zh: 他日，謂之曰：「朕即位以來，不輕與人改秩，今以命汝，異恩也。」

translations.literal: Another day the emperor said to him, "Since my accession I have not lightly granted rank changes. Today I bestow this on you—a special favor."
translations.idiomatic: Another day the emperor told him, "Since my accession I have rarely changed anyone's rank. This is a special honor."

sentences.zh: 檢正中書刑房，察訪淮浙常平、農田水利、差役事，還奏《役書》二十篇，加集賢校理。

translations.literal: He rectified the Criminal Section of the Secretariat, investigated ever-normal granaries, farmland and waterworks, and corvée service in Huai and Zhe, returned and submitted twenty chapters of the Corvée Book, and was given the additional title of Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He rectified the Secretariat's Criminal Section, investigated ever-normal granaries, waterworks, and corvée service in Huai and Zhe, submitted twenty chapters of the Corvée Book, and was made Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 又察訪陝西，時郡縣昧於奉法，斂羨餘過制。

translations.literal: He also investigated Shaanxi. At the time prefectures and counties were unclear about observing the law and collected surpluses beyond regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He also investigated Shaanxi, where prefectures and counties were collecting surpluses beyond what the law allowed.

sentences.zh: 承之曰：「是豈朝廷意邪？

translations.literal: Chengzhi said, "Is this the court's intent?"
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhi asked, "Is this what the court intends?"

sentences.zh: 」悉裁正其數。

translations.literal: He corrected all the figures.
translations.idiomatic: He corrected all the figures.

sentences.zh: 遷集賢殿修撰，擢寶文閣待制，為同群牧使，糾察在京刑獄兼樞密都承旨，出知延州，入權三司使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, elevated to Attendant Drafter of the Baowen Pavilion, served as Associate Commissioner of the Pasturage Office, investigated capital criminal cases while concurrently serving as Chief Secretariat Receiver of the Bureau of Military Affairs, went out as prefect of Yanzhou, and entered the capital as acting Commissioner of the Three Bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: He became Compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Attendant Drafter of the Baowen Pavilion, Associate Commissioner of the Pasturage Office, and investigator of capital criminal cases while also serving as Chief Secretariat Receiver of the Bureau of Military Affairs. He governed Yanzhou, then returned as acting Commissioner of the Three Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 蔡確治相州獄，多引朝士，皆望風自折服。

translations.literal: Cai Que handled the Xiangzhou case and implicated many court officials, who all bowed before the wind of his power.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Que handled the Xiangzhou case and implicated many court officials, who all submitted to his power.

sentences.zh: 承之為帝言其險詖之狀，帝意始悟，趣使詰竟。

translations.literal: Chengzhi told the emperor of his treacherous and perverse conduct. The emperor's mind was awakened and he hurriedly ordered the case pursued to its end.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhi described Cai's treacherous methods to the emperor, who came to his senses and ordered the case pursued to its conclusion.

sentences.zh: 遷龍圖閣直學士，懇辭，乞授兄肅之，曰：「臣少鞠於兄，且兄為待制十年矣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall. He earnestly declined and begged that the appointment be given to his elder brother Suzhi, saying, "Your servant was reared from childhood by my elder brother, and my brother has been an attendant drafter for ten years."
translations.idiomatic: He was made Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall but earnestly declined, asking that the post go to his elder brother Suzhi: "I was raised by my brother from childhood, and he has been an attendant drafter for ten years."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿兄弟孝友，足厲風俗。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "You brothers are filial and friendly—enough to admonish custom.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your brotherly devotion is an example to the realm.

sentences.zh: 肅之亦當遷也。

translations.literal: Suzhi should also be promoted."
translations.idiomatic: Suzhi should be promoted as well."

sentences.zh: 」即並命焉。

translations.literal: Both were appointed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Both were promoted at once.

sentences.zh: 商人犯禁貨北珠，乃為公主售，三司久不敢決。

translations.literal: A merchant violated the ban on northern pearls and sold them on behalf of a princess. The Three Bureaus long dared not decide the case.
translations.idiomatic: A merchant violated the ban on northern pearls by selling them for a princess, and the Three Bureaus long dared not decide the case.

sentences.zh: 承之曰：「朝廷法令，畏王姬乎？

translations.literal: Chengzhi said, "Are court laws to fear imperial princesses?"
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhi said, "Should the law fear an imperial princess?"

sentences.zh: 」亟索之。

translations.literal: He quickly demanded seizure of the goods.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the goods seized at once.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之曰：「有司當如此矣。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he said, "Officials ought to act like this."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it he said, "This is how officials ought to act."

sentences.zh: 」進樞密直學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 坐補吏不當，降待制、知汝州。

translations.literal: Because of improper appointment of clerks he was demoted to attendant drafter and made prefect of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After improper clerk appointments he was demoted to attendant drafter and made prefect of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為陝西都轉運使，召拜給事中、吏部侍郎、戶部尚書，復以樞密直學士知青州。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Director-General of Transport for Shaanxi, summoned and appointed Attendant Gentleman, Vice Minister of Personnel, and Minister of Revenue, and again made Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he headed transport in Shaanxi, was recalled as Attendant Gentleman, Vice Minister of Personnel, and Minister of Revenue, and again made Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 歷應天府、河陽、陳、鄆、揚州而卒。

translations.literal: He successively served at Yingtian, Heyang, Chen, Yan, and Yang prefectures and then died.
translations.idiomatic: He served at Yingtian, Heyang, Chen, Yan, and Yang prefectures and then died.

sentences.zh: 弟子 及之

translations.literal: Nephew: Jizhi
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Jizhi

sentences.zh: 及之，字公達，亦迪弟之子。

translations.literal: Jizhi, style name Gongda, was also a son of Di's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi, whose style name was Gongda, was likewise a son of Di's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 由蔭登第，通判安肅軍。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he entered the examination rolls and served as vice-commissioner of the Ansu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he entered office and served as vice-commissioner of the Ansu Army.

sentences.zh: 康定中，夏人犯邊，契丹復發兵並塞，疆候戒嚴。

translations.literal: In the Kangding era the Tangut violated the border and the Khitan again sent troops along the frontier. Border posts were placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangding era the Tangut raided the frontier and the Khitan again massed troops along the border, putting the frontier on alert.

sentences.zh: 及之言：「契丹以與夏人甥舅之故，特此慰其心，且姑張虛勢以疑我，必不失誓好，願毋過虞。

translations.literal: Jizhi said, "Because of the uncle-nephew tie between the Khitan and the Tangut, they are merely comforting them for the moment and for now displaying empty force to make us suspicious. They will certainly not break sworn friendship—please do not worry excessively."
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi said, "The Khitan are bound to the Tangut by marriage ties and are merely showing support while feigning strength to unsettle us. They will not break the alliance—please do not overreact."

sentences.zh: 」已而果然。

translations.literal: Before long it proved so.
translations.idiomatic: Events soon proved him right.

sentences.zh: 徙通判河南府。

translations.literal: He was transferred as vice-prefect of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred as vice-prefect of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 亡卒張海倚山嘯聚，白晝掠城市。

translations.literal: The deserter Zhang Hai gathered followers in the mountains and by day plundered cities.
translations.idiomatic: The deserter Zhang Hai gathered a band in the hills and raided cities in broad daylight.

sentences.zh: 及之督捕，單騎與海語，諭使歸命，當奏貸其死。

translations.literal: Jizhi supervised the hunt. Alone on horseback he spoke with Hai, urging him to surrender and promising to memorialize for sparing his life.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi led the pursuit, rode alone to parley with Hai, and promised to seek clemency if he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 海感動弛備，奏方上，而眾兵集，悉獲之。

translations.literal: Hai was moved and relaxed his guard. The memorial was just being sent up when troops gathered and all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Hai let down his guard. Before the memorial reached court, troops converged and captured the entire band.

sentences.zh: 知信州，靈鷲山浮屠，犯法者眾，及之治其奸，流數十人，乃自劾。

translations.literal: As prefect of Xinzhou, on Mount Lingjiu many monks broke the law. Jizhi punished their wrongdoing, banished several dozen, and then impeached himself.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Xinzhou he cracked down on lawless monks at Mount Lingjiu, banishing dozens, then impeached himself.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，釋不問。

translations.literal: The court praised him and released him without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised him and took no action against him.

sentences.zh: 入判刑部。

translations.literal: He entered the capital to judge cases in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital to judge cases in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 嘗撰次唐史有益治體者，為《君臣龜鑑》八十卷。

translations.literal: He once compiled passages from Tang history useful to governance into eighty chapters of Mirror for Ruler and Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled passages from Tang history useful to governance into the eighty-chapter Mirror for Ruler and Minister.

sentences.zh: 王堯臣上其書，並表其學行，韓琦亦以館職薦之。

translations.literal: Wang Yaochan presented the book to the throne and also praised his learning and conduct. Han Qi also recommended him for a post in the Hall of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yaochan presented the book and praised his scholarship; Han Qi also recommended him for a post in the Hall of Literature.

sentences.zh: 召試，除直秘閣，歷開封府判官、知涇、晉、陝三州。

translations.literal: He was summoned for examination, appointed to the Direct Secretariat Pavilion, and successively served as judge of Kaifeng and prefect of Jing, Jin, and Shan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for examination, he was appointed to the Direct Secretariat Pavilion and served as judge of Kaifeng and prefect of Jing, Jin, and Shan.

sentences.zh: 及之吏事精明，所居官皆稱職。

translations.literal: Jizhi was sharp in administrative affairs, and in every post he held he was considered competent.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi was sharp in administrative affairs and fulfilled every post competently.

sentences.zh: 以太中大夫致仕，再轉正議大夫。

translations.literal: He retired with the rank of Grand Master of Palace Administration and was later promoted to Right Grand Master of Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: He retired with the rank of Grand Master of Palace Administration and was later promoted to Right Grand Master of Discussion.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 柬之子孝基，及之子孝壽、孝稱。

translations.literal: Jian's son was Xiaoji; Jizhi's sons were Xiaoshou and Xiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi's son was Xiaoji; Jizhi's sons were Xiaoshou and Xiaocheng.

sentences.zh: 孫 孝基

translations.literal: Grandson: Xiaoji
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Xiaoji

sentences.zh: 孝基，字伯始。

translations.literal: Xiaoji, style name Boshi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoji, style name Boshi.

sentences.zh: 進士高第，唱名至墀下，仁宗顧侍臣曰：「此李迪孫邪？

translations.literal: He placed at the top rank in the jinshi examination and was called by name before the hall steps. Emperor Renzong turned to his attending ministers and said, "Is this not Li Di's grandson?
translations.idiomatic: He ranked at the top of the jinshi examination and was called by name before the hall steps. Emperor Renzong turned to his ministers and said, "Is this Li Di's grandson?

sentences.zh: 能世其家，可尚也。

translations.literal: He can carry on his family's tradition—worthy of respect."
translations.idiomatic: He can carry on the family tradition—worthy of esteem."

sentences.zh: 」晏殊、富弼薦其材任館閣，欲一見之。

translations.literal: Yan Shu and Fu Bi recommended his talents for service in the Hall of Literature and wished to meet him once.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shu and Fu Bi recommended his talents for a post in the Hall of Literature and wished to meet him.

sentences.zh: 孝基曰：「名器可私謁邪？

translations.literal: Xiaoji said, "Can official rank and office be sought through private visits?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoji said, "Can rank and office be sought through private visits?

sentences.zh: 」竟不往。

translations.literal: In the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not go.

sentences.zh: 知汝陰、雍丘縣，通判閬州、舒州，知隨州。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Ruyin and Yongqiu counties, vice-prefect of Lang and Shu prefectures, and prefect of Sui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Ruyin and Yongqiu counties, vice-prefect of Lang and Shu, and prefect of Sui.

sentences.zh: 所治雖劇，然事來亟斷，不為證左回枉，甫日中，庭已空矣。

translations.literal: Although the districts he governed were difficult, when cases came he decided them swiftly, did not allow evidence to be twisted to pervert justice, and by barely noon the court was already empty.
translations.idiomatic: Though his jurisdictions were demanding, he decided cases quickly without letting evidence be twisted; by mid-morning his courtroom was empty.

sentences.zh: 或問其術，曰：「無他，省事耳。

translations.literal: When asked his method, he said, "Nothing else—simply saving bother."
translations.idiomatic: When asked his secret, he said, "Nothing else—just cutting red tape."

sentences.zh: 」閬中江水齧城幾沒，郡吏多引避，孝基率其下決水歸旁谷，城賴以全。

translations.literal: In Lang, river water gnawed at the city wall until it nearly submerged it. Most prefectural officials avoided the danger, but Xiaoji led his subordinates to cut channels and return the water to side valleys, and the city was saved thereby.
translations.idiomatic: In Lang, the river nearly eroded the city wall away. Most officials fled, but Xiaoji led his men to divert the water into side channels and saved the city.

sentences.zh: 舒吏受賂鬻獄，以殺人罪加平民，孝基劾治三日，得其情，乃抵吏罪。

translations.literal: An official of Shu accepted bribes and sold justice, adding a murder charge to a commoner. Xiaoji investigated for three days, found the truth, and punished the official.
translations.idiomatic: A Shu official took bribes and framed a commoner for murder. Xiaoji investigated for three days, uncovered the truth, and punished the official.

sentences.zh: 以親須養，求監崇福宮，判西京國子監。

translations.literal: Because his parents required support, he requested supervision of Chongfu Palace and served as vice-director of the Western Capital Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: To care for his parents, he sought a post supervising Chongfu Palace and served as vice-director of the Western Capital Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 凡就閑十年，累官光祿卿，與父柬之同謝事，才年五十，士大夫美之，以比二疏。

translations.literal: In all he held idle posts for ten years, rose to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and resigned together with his father Jianzhi at the age of only fifty. The scholar-officials praised this, comparing them to the Two Shus.
translations.idiomatic: He spent ten years in honorary posts, rose to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and retired with his father Jianzhi at only fifty—scholar-officials praised them, comparing them to the Two Shus.

sentences.zh: 孝基為人沖澹，善養生，平居輕安。

translations.literal: Xiaoji was by nature unassuming and calm, skilled at nurturing life, and lived lightly and at ease in ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoji was unassuming and skilled at nurturing health; in daily life he lived lightly and at ease.

sentences.zh: 弟孝稱進對，帝問起居狀，歎曰：「度越常人遠矣。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xiaocheng entered audience. The emperor asked after Xiaoji's health and sighed, "He far surpasses ordinary men."
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiaocheng entered audience. The emperor asked after Xiaoji's health and sighed, "He far surpasses ordinary men."

sentences.zh: 」後十一年，無疾卒。

translations.literal: Eleven years later he died without illness.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven years later he died without illness.

sentences.zh: 孫 孝壽

translations.literal: Grandson: Xiaoshou
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Xiaoshou

sentences.zh: 前此，閭里亡賴子，自斷截臂腕，託廢疾淩良民，無所憚畏。

translations.literal: Before this, good-for-nothings in the neighborhoods cut off their own arms and wrists, pretended disability to bully law-abiding people, and feared nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, local ruffians mutilated their own limbs, feigned disability to bully upright citizens, and feared no one.

sentences.zh: 孝壽悉搜出之，部付旁郡，一切治理。

translations.literal: Xiaoshou searched them all out, dispatched them to neighboring prefectures, and cleaned up everything.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoshou rooted them all out, sent them to neighboring prefectures, and cleaned up the problem entirely.

sentences.zh: 加直學士，出知興仁、開德府。

translations.literal: He was made Academician Expositor and went out as prefect of Xingren and Kaide prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Made Academician Expositor, he served as prefect of Xingren and Kaide.

sentences.zh: 京起蘇州章綖獄，還孝壽開封，使往即訊。

translations.literal: Jing launched the Zhang Yan case in Suzhou and recalled Xiaoshou from Kaifeng, sending him to investigate immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing launched the Zhang Yan case in Suzhou and recalled Xiaoshou from Kaifeng to investigate at once.

sentences.zh: 至蘇州，窮治鑄錢，逮繫逾千數，方冬慘掠囚，墮指脫足不可計，死則投於垣外。

translations.literal: Reaching Suzhou, he exhaustively prosecuted coin-forging; over a thousand were arrested and imprisoned. It was deep winter and prisoners were cruelly tormented—countless lost fingers and toes to frostbite, and the dead were thrown outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: In Suzhou he ruthlessly prosecuted counterfeiting, arresting more than a thousand. In the harsh winter prisoners were tortured mercilessly; countless lost fingers and toes to frostbite, and the dead were cast outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 日夜鍛煉，疑未就，京猶嫌其緩，召使還。

translations.literal: Day and night he tortured them for confessions, but with doubts unresolved Jing still thought him too slow and summoned him back.
translations.idiomatic: He tortured prisoners day and night for confessions, but Cai Jing still found him too slow and recalled him.

sentences.zh: 其後，綖兄弟竟用此黥竄。

translations.literal: Afterward the Yan brothers were indeed tattooed and banished on this basis.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan brothers were ultimately tattooed and banished on the basis of this case.

sentences.zh: 又知虢、兗二州。

translations.literal: He also served as prefect of Guo and Yan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as prefect of Guo and Yan.

sentences.zh: 坐守興仁日與巡檢戲射狂人張立死，除名。

translations.literal: Because while guarding Xingren he daily played target-shooting with an inspector and a madman named Zhang Li died, he was stripped of his name from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: While prefect of Xingren he spent his days target-shooting with an inspector; when a madman named Zhang Li was killed, Xiaoshou was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 居無何，起知蘇州。

translations.literal: After no long time he was restored and made prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored and made prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 政和初，拜刑部侍郎，復改開封尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenghe era he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice and again made Prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhenghe era he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice and again made Prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 奉宸庫吏呂壽盜金，繫獄而逃。

translations.literal: Lu Shou, a clerk of the Imperial Attendant Storehouse, stole gold, was imprisoned, and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shou, a clerk of the Imperial Attendant Storehouse, stole gold, was imprisoned, and escaped.

sentences.zh: 孝壽盡執守兵，論為故縱，非任事之吏與不上直者，亦以不即追掩繩之。

translations.literal: Xiaoshou arrested all the guard soldiers, finding them guilty of deliberate release. Officials who were not on duty and guards not on active watch were also punished for failing to pursue and capture him at once.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoshou arrested every guard, charging deliberate negligence; even officials off duty and guards not on watch were punished for failing to pursue the fugitive immediately.

sentences.zh: 凡配隸四十人，陰賂杖者使加重，六七人才出關而死。

translations.literal: In all forty were banished to labor; secretly bribed to increase the beatings, six or seven died just after leaving the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Forty were sentenced to penal servitude; bribes secretly ensured heavier beatings, and six or seven died just after leaving the city.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，命悉還餘人。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he ordered the remainder all returned.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this, the emperor ordered the rest returned.

sentences.zh: 於是諫議大夫毛注論其殘忍苛虐，乞加譴，不聽。

translations.literal: Thereupon Remonstrance Official Mao Zhu denounced his cruelty and harshness and asked that he be punished, but the emperor did not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Official Mao Zhu denounced his cruelty and sought punishment, but the emperor ignored the request.

sentences.zh: 孝壽猶以獄空上表賀。

translations.literal: Xiaoshou still submitted a congratulatory memorial because the prisons were empty.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoshou still submitted a congratulatory memorial celebrating empty prisons.

sentences.zh: 孝壽雖亡狀，亦時有可觀。

translations.literal: Although Xiaoshou had disgraceful conduct, at times there was still something commendable.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xiaoshou was often disgraceful, at times he showed something commendable.

sentences.zh: 有舉子為僕所淩，忿甚，具牒欲送府，同舍生勸解，久乃釋。

translations.literal: An examination candidate was bullied by his servant and, furious, prepared a petition to send to the prefectural office. Fellow lodgers urged reconciliation, and only after a long time did he relent.
translations.idiomatic: An examination candidate was bullied by his servant and prepared a petition to the prefectural office in fury; fellow lodgers persuaded him to relent only after a long while.

sentences.zh: 戲取牒效孝壽花書判云：「不勘案，決杖二十。

translations.literal: In jest he took the petition and imitated Xiaoshou's florid signature with a judgment saying, "Without examining the case—sentence to twenty strokes of the rod."
translations.idiomatic: In jest he took the petition and forged Xiaoshou's florid signature with a judgment: "Without examining the case—twenty strokes of the rod."

sentences.zh: 」僕明日持詣府，告其主仿尹書判私用刑。

translations.literal: The next day the servant took it to the prefectural office and reported that his master had imitated the prefect's signature and privately inflicted punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the servant brought it to the prefectural office, accusing his master of forging the prefect's judgment and privately inflicting punishment.

sentences.zh: 孝壽即追至，備言本末，孝壽幡然曰：「所判正合我意。

translations.literal: Xiaoshou had him summoned at once. After the full story was told, Xiaoshou said with sudden change, "The judgment exactly accords with my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoshou had him summoned at once. After hearing the full story, Xiaoshou declared, "The judgment exactly matches my intent."

sentences.zh: 」如數與僕杖，而謝舉子。

translations.literal: He gave the servant the full number of strokes and apologized to the candidate.
translations.idiomatic: He gave the servant the full number of strokes and apologized to the candidate.

sentences.zh: 時都下數千人，無一僕敢肆者，時以此稱之。

translations.literal: At the time among several thousand in the capital not a single servant dared act outrageously, and people praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, among thousands in the capital not a single servant dared act outrageously, and people praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 明年，以疾，罷為龍圖閣學士、提舉醴泉觀。

translations.literal: The next year, on grounds of illness, he was dismissed and made Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall with charge of Liquan Abbey.
