translations.idiomatic: The next year, citing illness, he was dismissed and made Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall with charge of Liquan Abbey.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈正奉大夫。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given the rank of Right Grand Master of Submission.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously given the rank of Right Grand Master of Submission.

sentences.zh: 孫 孝稱

translations.literal: Grandson: Xiaocheng
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Xiaocheng

sentences.zh: 孝稱，字彥聞，以蔭登朝。

translations.literal: Xiaocheng, style name Yanwen, entered court through hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaocheng, style name Yanwen, entered court through hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 值郊恩得封父，及之已官通議大夫，有司限以格，孝稱言，恐非朝廷所以推恩優老之意，詔特許之，遂為著令。

translations.literal: When a suburban sacrifice grace allowed ennobling one's father, Jizhi already held the rank of Grand Master of Discussion. The relevant offices restricted this by regulation. Xiaocheng argued that this likely did not accord with the court's intent to extend grace and honor the aged. An edict specially permitted it, and this became established regulation.
translations.idiomatic: During a suburban sacrifice amnesty that permitted ennobling one's father, Jizhi already held the rank of Grand Master of Discussion. Officials blocked it on regulatory grounds, but Xiaocheng argued this thwarted the court's intent to honor the aged. The emperor granted an exception, and it became permanent law.

sentences.zh: 崇寧中，提舉湖北、京西常平，提點京西南路刑獄。

translations.literal: During the Chongning era he was put in charge of the Hubei and Jingxi Ever-Normal Granaries and served as intendant of criminal cases on the Southwest Jing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongning era he oversaw the Hubei and Jingxi Ever-Normal Granaries and served as intendant of criminal cases on the Southwest Jing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 蔡京之姻宋喬年為京畿轉運使，有囚逸，捕得之。

translations.literal: Song Qiaonian, a relation by marriage of Cai Jing, was transport commissioner of the Capital Region. A prisoner escaped and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiaonian, Cai Jing's relation by marriage and transport commissioner of the Capital Region, recaptured an escaped prisoner.

sentences.zh: 孝稱上其功，喬年受賞，而孝稱用是得工部員外郎。

translations.literal: Xiaocheng reported his achievement. Qiaonian received reward, and Xiaocheng thereby obtained the post of Outer Section Member of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaocheng reported the achievement; Qiaonian was rewarded, and Xiaocheng thereby obtained the post of Outer Section Member of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 不閱月，遷大理少卿。

translations.literal: In less than a month he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In less than a month he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 連奏獄空，進為卿，且數增秩，擢工部、戶部二侍郎，為開封尹。

translations.literal: He repeatedly reported empty prisons, was promoted to director, received several rank increases, was elevated to Vice Minister of Works and Vice Minister of Revenue, and made Prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly reported empty prisons, rose to director, received several rank increases, was elevated to Vice Minister of Works and Vice Minister of Revenue, and made Prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 陳瓘之子正彙在杭州上書，告京不利社稷。

translations.literal: Zhenghui, son of Chen Guan, submitted a memorial at Hangzhou accusing Jing of harming the state.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guan's son Zhenghui submitted a memorial from Hangzhou accusing Cai Jing of harming the state.

sentences.zh: 郡守蔡薿執送京師，並逮瓘詣獄，孝稱脅使證其子，瓘不可。

translations.literal: Prefect Cai Ni arrested and sent him to the capital, and Chen Guan was also seized and brought to prison. Xiaocheng coerced him to testify against his son, but Chen Guan refused.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Cai Ni arrested Zhenghui and sent him to the capital; Chen Guan was also seized and imprisoned. Xiaocheng coerced Chen Guan to testify against his son, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 暨獄上，竟竄正彙海島。

translations.literal: When the case was finalized, Zhenghui was banished to an island at sea.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was finalized, Zhenghui was banished to an island at sea.

sentences.zh: 京愈德之，進刑部尚書，而以其兄孝壽代為尹。

translations.literal: Jing was all the more grateful and promoted him to Minister of Justice, appointing his elder brother Xiaoshou to replace him as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing was all the more grateful and promoted him to Minister of Justice, appointing his elder brother Xiaoshou to replace him as prefect.

sentences.zh: 孝稱請班兄下，不許。

translations.literal: Xiaocheng asked to rank below his elder brother but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaocheng asked to rank below his elder brother but was refused.

sentences.zh: 避親嫌，徙工部。

translations.literal: To avoid conflict of interest with a relative, he was moved to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid conflict of interest with a relative, he was transferred to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously given the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 王曾，字孝先，青州益都人。

translations.literal: Wang Zeng, style name Xiaoxian, was a native of Yidu in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zeng, style name Xiaoxian, was a native of Yidu in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，鞠於仲父宗元，從學於里人張震，善為文辭。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was raised by his father's younger brother Zongyuan, studied under the local scholar Zhang Zhen, and was skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was raised by his uncle Zongyuan and studied under the local scholar Zhang Zhen, excelling in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，由鄉貢試禮部、廷對皆第一。

translations.literal: During the Xianping era, through the provincial tribute he ranked first in both the Ministry of Rites examination and the palace audience.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping era he ranked first in both the Ministry of Rites examination and the palace audience after passing the provincial tribute.

sentences.zh: 楊億見其賦，歎曰：「王佐器也。

translations.literal: Yang Yi saw his rhapsody and sighed, "Material for assisting a ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi read his rhapsody and sighed, "Material for a king's minister."

sentences.zh: 」以將作監丞通判濟州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and vice-prefect of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and vice-prefect of Ji.

sentences.zh: 代還，當召試學士院，宰相寇準奇之，特試政事堂，授秘書省著作郎、直史館、三司戶部判官。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned, he was to be summoned for examination at the Academy of Letters. Chief Councillor Kou Zhun marveled at him, had him specially examined at the Council Chamber, and appointed him Compiler in the Secretariat, Keeper of the Historiography Institute, and Section Chief of the Three Bureaus Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, he was to be examined at the Academy of Letters. Chief Councillor Kou Zhun was impressed and had him examined in the Council Chamber, appointing him Compiler in the Secretariat, Keeper of the Historiography Institute, and Section Chief of the Three Bureaus Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 景德初，始通和契丹，歲遣使致書稱南朝，以契丹為北朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingde era peace was first established with the Khitan. Each year envoys were sent with letters calling the Song the Southern Court and the Khitan the Northern Court.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was first established with the Khitan in the Jingde era, annual envoys addressed letters calling the Song the Southern Court and the Khitan the Northern Court.

sentences.zh: 曾曰：「從其國號足矣。

translations.literal: Zeng said, "It is enough to use their state name."
translations.idiomatic: Zeng said, "It is enough to use their state name."

sentences.zh: 」業已遣使，弗果易。

translations.literal: Envoys had already been sent, and the wording was not in the end changed.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys had already been dispatched, and the wording was not changed.

sentences.zh: 遷右正言、知制誥兼史館修撰。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Remonstrance Official, Drafter of Imperial Edicts, and concurrently Compiler of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Remonstrance Official, Drafter of Imperial Edicts, and concurrently Compiler of the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 時瑞應遝至，曾嘗入對，帝語及之，曾奏曰：「此誠國家承平所致，然願推而弗居，異日或有災沴，則免輿議。

translations.literal: At the time auspicious omens arrived in succession. Zeng once entered audience; the emperor spoke of them, and Zeng memorialized, "This is truly due to the nation's peace and stability, yet I hope Your Majesty will extend it but not take credit. If disaster should come another day, public blame may be avoided."
translations.idiomatic: As auspicious omens multiplied, Zeng once addressed the emperor, who spoke of them. Zeng said, "This reflects the nation's peace, yet I hope Your Majesty will accept the blessing without claiming credit—if disaster comes later, you will avoid public blame."

sentences.zh: 」及帝既受符命，大建玉清昭應宮，下莫敢言者，曾陳五害以諫。

translations.literal: When the emperor had received the Heavenly mandate and built the Jade Pure Temple of Corresponding Response on a grand scale, none below dared speak out. Zeng set forth five harms in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor received the Heavenly mandate and undertook the grand construction of the Jade Pure Temple of Corresponding Response, none dared object. Zeng listed five harms in remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 舊用郎中官判大理寺，帝欲重之，特命曾。

translations.literal: Formerly a Langzhong official judged the Court of Judicial Review; the emperor wished to give it weight and specially appointed Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review had formerly been overseen by a Langzhong official; the emperor wished to elevate the post and specially appointed Zeng.

sentences.zh: 且謂曾曰：「獄，重典也，今以屈卿。

translations.literal: He also said to Zeng, "Prisons are a weighty institution—today I must demean you."
translations.idiomatic: He also said to Zeng, "Prisons are a weighty institution—today I must demean you."

sentences.zh: 」曾頓首謝。

translations.literal: Zeng bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng bowed his head in thanks.

sentences.zh: 仍賜錢三十萬，因請自辟僚屬，著為令。

translations.literal: He was also granted three hundred thousand cash and requested to appoint his own staff; this was established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted three hundred thousand cash and received permission to appoint his own staff—a rule thereafter written into law.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗晚坐承明殿，召對久之，既退，使內侍諭曰：「向思卿甚，故不及朝服見卿，卿勿以我為慢也。

translations.literal: The emperor once sat late in Chengmeng Hall and summoned him for a long audience. After he withdrew, he had a palace attendant convey, "I was thinking of you greatly just now, and so did not wait to don court robes before seeing you—do not take me as discourteous."
translations.idiomatic: One evening the emperor sat late in Chengmeng Hall and held a long audience with Zeng. After Zeng withdrew, a palace attendant conveyed the emperor's words: "I had you much in mind and did not wait to don court robes—please do not think me discourteous."

sentences.zh: 」其見尊禮如此。

translations.literal: Such was the honor and courtesy shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the honor and courtesy shown him.

sentences.zh: 知審刑院。

translations.literal: He served as director of the Office of Criminal Review.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director of the Office of Criminal Review.

sentences.zh: 舊違制無故失，率坐徒二年，曾請須親被旨乃坐。

translations.literal: Formerly, violation of regulations without cause was uniformly punished by two years of penal servitude. Zeng requested that guilt be found only when one had personally received the imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, violating regulations without explicit authorization was uniformly punished by two years of penal servitude. Zeng argued punishment should apply only when one had personally received an imperial order.

sentences.zh: 既而有犯者，曾乃以失論。

translations.literal: When a violator soon appeared, Zeng judged it as mere negligence.
translations.idiomatic: When a violation occurred, Zeng classified it as negligent error rather than deliberate breach.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「如卿言，是無復有違制者。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "As you say, then there would never again be violators of regulations."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "By your reasoning, there would never again be violators of regulations."

sentences.zh: 」曾曰：「天下至廣，豈人人盡曉制書，如陛下言，亦無復有失者。

translations.literal: Zeng said, "The realm is vast—can every man fully understand regulatory texts? By Your Majesty's reasoning, there would also never again be offenders through error."
translations.idiomatic: Zeng said, "The realm is vast—can every man fully understand the regulations? By Your Majesty's reasoning, there would also never again be offenders through error."

sentences.zh: 」帝悟，卒從曾議。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and in the end followed Zeng's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and in the end adopted Zeng's proposal.

sentences.zh: 再遷尚書主客郎中。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Langzhong of the Ministry of Rites Guest Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to Langzhong of the Ministry of Rites Guest Section.

sentences.zh: 知審官院、通進銀臺司，勾當三班院，遂以右諫議大夫參知政事。

translations.literal: He served as director of the Office of Merit Evaluation, the Memorial Clearance and Silver Terrace Office, and the Office of the Three Ranks, and thereby became Right Remonstrance Grandee and Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He directed the Office of Merit Evaluation, the Memorial Clearance and Silver Terrace Office, and the Office of the Three Ranks, then became Right Remonstrance Grandee and Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 時宮觀皆以輔臣為使。

translations.literal: At the time palace abbeys were all headed by chief ministers as commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: At the time palace abbeys were all headed by chief ministers as commissioners.

sentences.zh: 王欽若方挾符瑞，傅會帝意，又陰欲排異己者，曾當使會靈，因以推欽若，帝始疑曾自異。

translations.literal: Wang Qinruo was just then wielding portents to flatter the emperor's wishes and secretly sought to drive out those who differed. Zeng was to serve as commissioner of the Abbey of Congregated Spirits and therefore yielded the post to Qinruo. The emperor began to suspect that Zeng opposed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo was exploiting portents to flatter the emperor and secretly sought to purge rivals. Zeng was due to head the Abbey of Congregated Spirits but yielded the post to Qinruo; the emperor began to suspect Zeng of dissent.

sentences.zh: 及欽若相，會曾市賀皇后家舊第，其家未徙去，而曾令人舁土置門外，賀氏訴禁中。

translations.literal: When Qinruo became chief councillor, it happened that Zeng bought the former residence of Empress He. The family had not yet moved out, yet Zeng had earth piled at the gate. The He family complained within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinruo became chief councillor, Zeng bought Empress He's former residence while her family still occupied it and had earth piled at their gate. The He family complained to the palace.

sentences.zh: 明日，帝以語欽若，乃罷曾為尚書禮部侍郎、判都省，出知應天府。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor told Qinruo; Zeng was removed as Vice Minister of Rites in the Ministry of Rites and director of the Department of State Affairs, and sent out as prefect of Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor told Qinruo; Zeng was removed as Vice Minister of Rites and director of the Department of State Affairs and sent out as prefect of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 天禧中，民間訛言有妖起若飛帽，夜搏人，自京師以南，人皆恐。

translations.literal: During the Tianxi era, a rumor spread among the people that a demon shaped like a flying cap arose and seized people by night. From the capital southward all were fearful.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianxi era rumor spread of a demon like a flying cap that seized people at night; from the capital southward the populace was terrified.

sentences.zh: 曾令夜開里門，敢倡言者即捕之，卒無妖。

translations.literal: Zeng ordered the neighborhood gates opened at night and had anyone who dared spread the rumor arrested at once. In the end there was no demon.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng ordered neighborhood gates kept open at night and had rumor-mongers arrested; in the end no demon appeared.

sentences.zh: 徙天雄軍，復參知政事，遷吏部侍郎兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Tianxiong Army, again became Vice Grand Councillor, and was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrently Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Tianxiong Army, again became Vice Grand Councillor, and was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel and Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 真宗不豫，皇后居中預政，太子雖聽事資善堂，然事皆決於后，中外以為憂。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong fell ill, the empress held sway at court in advance of government. Although the crown prince heard cases at the Hall of Cultivating Virtue, all affairs were decided by the empress; inside and outside the court were concerned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong fell ill, the empress effectively governed from within the palace. Though the crown prince held audiences at the Hall of Cultivating Virtue, the empress decided all affairs—a source of worry throughout the court.

sentences.zh: 錢惟演，后戚也，曾密語惟演曰：「太子幼，非宮中不能立。

translations.literal: Qian Weiyan was a relative of the empress. Zeng secretly told Weiyan, "The crown prince is young; without the palace he cannot be established."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Weiyan was a relative of the empress. Zeng secretly told Weiyan, "The crown prince is young; without the palace he cannot be established."

sentences.zh: 加恩太子，則太子安；

translations.literal: If favors are added for the crown prince, then the crown prince will be secure;
translations.idiomatic: If favors are granted the crown prince, the crown prince will be secure;

sentences.zh: 太子安，所以安劉氏也。

translations.literal: if the crown prince is secure, that is how the Liu family will be secure.
translations.idiomatic: if the crown prince is secure, the Liu family will be secure as well.

sentences.zh: 」惟演以為然，因以白后。

translations.literal: Weiyan thought it correct and thereby reported it to the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyan agreed and reported it to the empress.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，曾奉命入殿廬草遺詔：「以明肅皇后輔立皇太子，權聽斷軍國大事。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Zeng received orders to enter the mourning hall and draft the final edict: "Let Empress Mingsu assist in establishing the crown prince and provisionally hear and decide the great affairs of state and army."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, Zeng was ordered into the mourning hall to draft the final edict: "Let Empress Mingsu assist in establishing the crown prince and provisionally decide the great affairs of state and military."

sentences.zh: 」丁謂入，去「權」字。

translations.literal: Ding Wei entered and removed the character "provisionally."
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei entered and struck the word "provisionally."

sentences.zh: 曾曰：「皇帝沖年，太后臨朝，斯已國家否運。

translations.literal: Zeng said, "The emperor is in his tender years and the empress dowager holds court—this is already the nation's ill fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Zeng said, "The emperor is still a child and the empress dowager already holds court—surely this is the realm's ill fortune."

sentences.zh: 稱『權』，猶足示後。

translations.literal: To use the term "provisionally" still suffices to instruct posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Retaining the word "provisionally" would still be enough to instruct posterity.

sentences.zh: 且增減制書有法，表則之地，先欲亂之邪？

translations.literal: Moreover, adding to or subtracting from imperial edicts has established law—is this the place that sets the standard, and do you first wish to throw it into disorder?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, altering imperial edicts is governed by law—this is the very place that sets the standard; do you wish to throw protocol into disorder?

sentences.zh: 」遂不敢去。

translations.literal: So he did not dare remove it.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei then did not dare remove it.

sentences.zh: 仁宗立，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong ascended, Zeng was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong ascended, Zeng was made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 群臣議太后臨朝儀，曾請如東漢故事，太后坐帝右，垂簾奏事，丁謂獨欲帝朔望見群臣，大事則太后召對輔臣決之，非大事，令入內押班雷允恭傳奏禁中，畫可以下。

translations.literal: When the officials deliberated on the protocol for the empress dowager's regency, Zeng requested following Eastern Han precedent: the empress dowager would sit to the emperor's right behind a screen and curtain to hear and decide affairs. Ding Wei alone wanted the emperor to see officials on the first and fifteenth of the month; for great matters the empress dowager would summon and confer with chief ministers to decide; for non-great matters, he would have Inner Attendant Ban Officer Lei Yonggong transmit memorials within the palace, and minor matters could be delegated downward.
translations.idiomatic: When officials debated regency protocol, Zeng urged following Eastern Han precedent: the empress dowager would sit to the emperor's right behind a screen to hear affairs. Ding Wei alone wanted the emperor to receive officials on the first and fifteenth of each month; major matters would be decided when the empress dowager summoned chief ministers, while lesser affairs would be relayed within the palace by Lei Yonggong, Inner Attendant Ban Officer, with minor matters handled at lower levels.

sentences.zh: 曾曰：「兩宮異處，而柄歸宦官，禍端兆矣。

translations.literal: Zeng said, "The two palaces in separate places while power falls to eunuchs—the augury of disaster has appeared."
translations.idiomatic: Zeng said, "With the two palaces apart and power in eunuch hands, disaster is already foreshadowed."

sentences.zh: 」謂不聽。

translations.literal: Wei did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 既而允恭坐誅，謂亦得罪。

translations.literal: Before long Yonggong was punished with execution, and Wei also suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yonggong was executed for his crimes, and Ding Wei was punished as well.

sentences.zh: 自是兩宮垂簾，輔臣奏事如曾議。

translations.literal: From then on both palaces sat behind the screen, and chief ministers reported affairs as Zeng had proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter both palaces heard affairs from behind the screen, with chief ministers reporting as Zeng had urged.

sentences.zh: 謂初敗，任中正言：「謂被先帝顧託，雖有罪，請如律議功。

translations.literal: When Wei first fell, Ren Zhongzheng said, "Wei received the late emperor's entrustment; though guilty, I ask that his merits be weighed according to law."
translations.idiomatic: When Ding Wei first fell, Ren Zhongzheng said, "He received the late emperor's trust; though guilty, please weigh his merits according to law."

sentences.zh: 」曾曰：「謂以不忠得罪宗廟，尚何議邪！

translations.literal: Zeng said, "Wei offended the imperial ancestors through disloyalty—what is there still to discuss!"
translations.idiomatic: Zeng said, "Ding Wei offended the imperial ancestors through disloyalty—what merits remain to discuss!"

sentences.zh: 」時真宗初崩，內外洶洶，曾正色獨立，朝廷倚以為重。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Zhenzong had just died; inside and outside the court were in turmoil. Zeng alone stood with stern countenance, and the court relied on him as a pillar.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong had just died and the court was in turmoil, Zeng alone stood firm; the court leaned heavily on him.

sentences.zh: 拜中書侍郎兼本官、同中書門下平章事、集賢殿大學士、會靈觀使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat while retaining his current rank, Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling Worthies, and Commissioner of the Abbey of Congregated Spirits.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat while retaining his current rank, Grand Councillor, Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling Worthies, and Commissioner of the Abbey of Congregated Spirits.

sentences.zh: 王欽若卒，曾以門下侍郎兼戶部尚書為昭文館大學士、監修國史、玉清昭應宮使。

translations.literal: When Wang Qinruo died, Zeng served as Vice Minister of the Chancellery and concurrently Minister of Revenue as Grand Academician of the Hall of Glorious Literature, Supervisor of the Compilation of the National History, and Commissioner of the Palace of Jade Purity and Resonance with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Qinruo died, Zeng became Grand Academician of the Hall of Glorious Literature, Supervisor of the National History, and Commissioner of the Palace of Jade Purity and Resonance with Heaven, while serving as Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 曾以帝初即位，宜近師儒，即召孫奭、馮元勸講崇政殿。

translations.literal: Zeng, considering that the emperor had just ascended and ought to be near scholar-teachers, immediately summoned Sun Shi and Feng Yuan to lecture at the Hall of Honoring Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Believing the newly enthroned emperor should be close to scholar-teachers, Zeng immediately summoned Sun Shi and Feng Yuan to lecture at the Hall of Honoring Governance.

sentences.zh: 天聖四年夏，大雨，傳言汴口決，水且大至，都人恐，欲東奔。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiansheng, summer, there was heavy rain. Rumor spread that the Bian River mouth had broken and great floods were coming; the capital populace feared and wished to flee east.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year of Tiansheng, heavy rains fueled rumors that the Bian River had breached and a great flood was coming; the people of the capital panicked and prepared to flee east.

sentences.zh: 帝問曾，曾曰：「河決奏未至，第民間妖言爾，不足慮也。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Zeng. Zeng said, "No report of a river breach has arrived; it is only folk rumor—not worth concern."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Zeng, who replied, "No report of a river breach has arrived—it is only rumor among the people and not worth concern."

sentences.zh: 」已而果然。

translations.literal: Before long this proved true indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Events soon confirmed he was right.

sentences.zh: 陝西轉過使置醋務，以榷其利，且請推其法天下，曾請罷之。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi transport commissioner established a vinegar monopoly office to corner its profits and also requested extending this method empire-wide. Zeng requested its abolition.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi transport commissioner set up a vinegar monopoly to seize its profits and sought to extend the scheme empire-wide; Zeng petitioned for its abolition.

sentences.zh: 曾方嚴持重，每進見，言利害事，審而中理；

translations.literal: Zeng was stern and weighty in bearing. Whenever he entered audience, he spoke on matters of benefit and harm with careful and sound reasoning;
translations.idiomatic: Zeng was stern and dignified; whenever he entered audience he spoke on matters of public interest with careful, sound reasoning;

sentences.zh: 多所薦拔，尤惡僥幸。

translations.literal: he recommended and promoted many men and especially hated those who sought advancement through luck and favor.
translations.idiomatic: he recommended and promoted many men and especially despised those who sought advancement through favor and luck.

sentences.zh: 帝問曾曰：「比臣僚請對，多求進者。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Zeng, "Recently when officials requested audience, many were seeking advancement."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Zeng, "Lately when officials request audience, many are seeking promotion."

sentences.zh: 」曾對曰：「惟陛下抑奔競而崇恬靜，庶幾有難進易退之人矣。

translations.literal: Zeng replied, "If Your Majesty restrains eager rivalry and honors quiet integrity, perhaps there will be men slow to advance and quick to withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: Zeng replied, "If Your Majesty restrains eager rivalry and honors quiet integrity, perhaps there will be men slow to seek office and quick to retire."

sentences.zh: 」曹利用惡曾班己上，嘗怏怏不悅，語在《利用傳》。

translations.literal: Cao Liyong resented that Zeng outranked him and was often displeased; the account is in the Biography of Liyong.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Liyong resented that Zeng outranked him and was often displeased; the account appears in his biography.

sentences.zh: 及利用坐事，太后大怒，曾為之解。

translations.literal: When Liyong was implicated in a crime, the empress dowager was greatly angered; Zeng pleaded on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When Liyong was implicated in wrongdoing, the empress dowager was furious; Zeng pleaded on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「卿嘗言利用強橫，今何解也？

translations.literal: The empress dowager said, "You once said Liyong was overbearing—why do you plead for him now?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "You once said Liyong was overbearing—why do you plead for him now?"

sentences.zh: 」曾曰：「利用素恃恩，臣故嘗以理折之。

translations.literal: Zeng said, "Liyong has long relied on favor; I therefore sometimes rebutted him with reason."
translations.idiomatic: Zeng said, "Liyong has long relied on imperial favor; I therefore sometimes rebutted him with reason."

sentences.zh: 今加以大惡，則非臣所知也。

translations.literal: Now that great wickedness is added, that is not something I knew.
translations.idiomatic: As for the grave crimes now charged against him, those were not known to me.

sentences.zh: 」太后意少釋，卒從輕議。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's anger eased somewhat, and in the end a lighter sentence was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's anger eased somewhat, and in the end a lighter sentence was adopted.

sentences.zh: 始，太后受冊，將御大安殿，曾執以為不可，及長寧節上壽，止供張便殿。

translations.literal: At first, when the empress dowager received her patent of investiture and was about to ascend the Hall of Great Peace, Zeng insisted it was improper; when celebrating her birthday at Changning, only the convenient hall was furnished.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager first received her investiture and was about to hold court in the Hall of Great Peace, Zeng objected; for her Changning birthday celebration, only a side hall was prepared.

sentences.zh: 太后左右姻家稍通請謁，曾多所裁抑，太后滋不悅。

translations.literal: Relatives of those around the empress dowager gradually gained access through petitions; Zeng frequently cut them off, and the empress dowager grew ever more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives of the empress dowager's attendants gradually gained access through petitions; Zeng frequently blocked them, and the empress dowager grew ever more displeased.

sentences.zh: 會玉清昭應宮災，乃出知青州。

translations.literal: When the Palace of Jade Purity and Resonance with Heaven burned, he was sent out as prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Palace of Jade Purity and Resonance with Heaven burned, he was sent out as prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以彰信軍節度使復知天雄軍，契丹使者往還，斂車徒而後過，無敢嘩者。

translations.literal: Made military commissioner of Zhangxin Army and again prefect of Tianxiong Army, when Khitan envoys passed back and forth they restrained their carriages and followers before passing—none dared make a disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: As military commissioner of Zhangxin Army he again governed Tianxiong Army; when Khitan envoys passed through, they quieted their carriages and followers before proceeding—none dared cause a disturbance.

sentences.zh: 人樂其政，為畫像而生祠之。

translations.literal: The people rejoiced in his governance and painted his portrait and worshipped him in life.
translations.idiomatic: The people rejoiced in his governance and painted his portrait, worshipping him while he still lived.

sentences.zh: 改天平軍節度使、同中書門下平章事、判河南府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner of Tianping Army, Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and administrator of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military commissioner of Tianping Army, Grand Councillor, and administrator of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 景祐元年，為樞密使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyou, he became Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingyou, he became Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜右僕射兼門下侍郎、平章事、集賢殿大學士，封沂國公。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Vice Minister of the Chancellery, Grand Councillor, Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling Worthies, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Vice Minister of the Chancellery, Grand Councillor, Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling Worthies, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yi.

sentences.zh: 曾資質端厚，眉目如畫。

translations.literal: Zeng's character was upright and solid; his brows and eyes were as if painted.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng was upright and solid in character, with brows and eyes fine as a painting.

sentences.zh: 在朝廷，進止皆有常處，平居寡言笑，人莫敢干以私。

translations.literal: At court his comings and goings always had fixed places; in ordinary life he spoke little and laughed little—no one dared approach him with private requests.
translations.idiomatic: At court his movements always followed fixed places; in daily life he spoke and laughed little, and no one dared approach him with private requests.

sentences.zh: 少與楊億同在侍從，億喜談謔，凡僚友無不狎侮。

translations.literal: In youth he was together with Yang Yi among attendants; Yi loved jesting talk and would familiarly mock every colleague without exception.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served alongside Yang Yi among the emperor's attendants; Yi loved banter and familiarly mocked every colleague without exception.

sentences.zh: 至與曾言，則曰：「余不敢以戲也。

translations.literal: But when speaking with Zeng he would say, "I dare not treat it as jest."
translations.idiomatic: But when speaking with Zeng he would say, "I dare not treat it as jest."

sentences.zh: 」平生自奉甚儉，有故人子孫京來告別，曾留之具饌，食後，合中送數軸簡紙，啟視之，皆它人書簡後裁取者也。

translations.literal: Throughout life he was very frugal in his personal upkeep. Once a friend's descendant Jing came to bid farewell; Zeng kept him and set out food. After the meal, his clerk sent several scrolls of letter paper; opening them, all were cut from the backs of others' letters.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout life he was very frugal. Once a friend's descendant named Jing came to bid farewell; Zeng kept him and served a meal. Afterward his clerk sent several scrolls of letter paper—all of it cut from the blank backs of other people's letters.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，仁宗為篆其碑曰「旌賢之碑」，後又改其鄉曰旌賢鄉。

translations.literal: During Huangyou, Emperor Renzong personally wrote in seal script on his stele "Stele Honoring the Worthy," and later renamed his township Worthy Honor Township.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangyou, Emperor Renzong personally inscribed his stele in seal script with the words "Stele Honoring the Worthy," and later renamed his township Worthy Honor Township.

sentences.zh: 大臣賜碑篆自曾始。

translations.literal: The bestowal of seal-script stele inscriptions upon grand ministers began with Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial bestowal of seal-script stele inscriptions upon grand ministers began with Zeng.

sentences.zh: 仁宗既祔廟，詔擇將相配享，以曾為第一。

translations.literal: After Emperor Renzong was enshrined in the ancestral temple, an edict selected generals and ministers for paired offerings; Zeng was ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Renzong was enshrined in the ancestral temple, an edict selected generals and ministers for paired offerings; Zeng was ranked first.

sentences.zh: 曾無子，養子曰縡。

translations.literal: Zeng had no sons; his adopted son was named Zao.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng had no sons; his adopted son was named Zao.

sentences.zh: 又以弟子融之子繹為後，尚書兵部郎中、秘閣校理致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He also took his younger brother Zirong's son Yi as heir. Yi served as Langzhong in the Ministry of War Personnel Section and collator in the Secret Archive, retired, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He also made his younger brother Zirong's son Yi his heir. Yi served as Langzhong in the Ministry of War and as collator in the Secret Archive, retired, and died.

sentences.zh: 弟 子融

translations.literal: Younger brother: Zirong
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Zirong

sentences.zh: 子融，字熙仲。

translations.literal: Zirong, style name Xizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zirong, whose style name was Xizhong,

sentences.zh: 初以曾奏，為將作監主簿。

translations.literal: At first through Zeng's memorial he was made principal clerk of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: At first, through Zeng's memorial, he was appointed principal clerk of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 祥符進士及第，累遷太常丞、同知禮院。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the Xiangfu era and was successively promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Associate Director of the Ritual Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the jinshi examination in the Xiangfu era, he rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Associate Director of the Ritual Institute.

sentences.zh: 獻所為文，召試，直集賢院。

translations.literal: He presented his writings, was summoned for examination, and appointed to the Hall for Assembling Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He presented his writings, was summoned for examination, and appointed to the Hall for Assembling Worthies.

sentences.zh: 嘗論次國朝以來典禮因革，為《禮閣新編》上之。

translations.literal: He once arranged the changes in ceremonial rites since the founding of the dynasty and presented New Compilation of the Ritual Hall to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He once compiled the changes in ceremonial rites since the founding of the dynasty and presented the New Compilation of the Ritual Hall to the throne.

sentences.zh: 以其書藏太常。

translations.literal: His book was stored in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His book was deposited in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 權三司度支、鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: Acting Revenue and Salt and Iron Commissioner of the Three Bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting Revenue and Salt and Iron Commissioner of the Three Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 任布請鑄大錢，行之京城。

translations.literal: Ren Bu requested casting large coins and implementing them in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Bu proposed casting large coins and circulating them in the capital.

sentences.zh: 三司使程琳集官議，子融曰：「今軍營半在城外，獨行大錢城中，可乎？

translations.literal: Three Bureaus Commissioner Cheng Lin assembled officials to deliberate. Zirong said, "Now half the garrisons are outside the walls—can large coins alone circulate within the city?"
translations.idiomatic: Three Bureaus Commissioner Cheng Lin assembled officials to discuss the proposal. Zirong said, "Half the garrisons are now outside the walls—can large coins circulate in the city alone?"

sentences.zh: 」事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was then dropped.

sentences.zh: 權同糾察刑獄、知河陽。

translations.literal: Acting Co-Inspector of Criminal Cases and prefect of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting Co-Inspector of Criminal Cases and prefect of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 又集五代事，為《唐餘錄》六十卷以獻。

translations.literal: He also collected events of the Five Dynasties period into sixty chapters of Records of Tang Remnants and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He also collected events of the Five Dynasties into the sixty-chapter Records of Tang Remnants and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 進直龍圖閣，累遷太常少卿、權判大理寺。

translations.literal: Promoted to Direct Attendant of the Dragon Diagram Hall; successively promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and acting chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Direct Attendant of the Dragon Diagram Hall, he rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and acting chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 乃取讞獄輕重可為準者，類次以為斷例。

translations.literal: He then selected criminal cases whose severity could serve as standards, classified them, and made them precedents for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: He then selected criminal cases whose severity could serve as standards, classified them, and compiled them as precedents for judgment.

sentences.zh: 拜天章閣待制、尚書吏部郎中、知荊南。

translations.literal: Appointed Attendant Drafting in the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations, Langzhong in the Ministry of Personnel, and prefect of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant Drafting in the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations, Langzhong in the Ministry of Personnel, and prefect of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 盜張海縱掠襄、鄧，至荊門，子融閱州兵，將迎擊之，賊引去。

translations.literal: The bandit Zhang Hai ranged through Xiang and Deng and reached Jingmen. Zirong reviewed prefectural troops and was about to meet and strike him; the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Zhang Hai raided through Xiang and Deng and reached Jingmen. Zirong reviewed prefectural troops and prepared to meet and strike him; the bandits withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遷右諫議大夫、知陝州，徙河中府。

translations.literal: Promoted to Right Remonstrance Grandee and prefect of Shaanzhou; transferred to Hezhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Right Remonstrance Grandee and prefect of Shaanzhou, he was later transferred to Hezhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既而勾當三班院，遷給事中，以尚書工部侍郎、集賢院學士知兗州。

translations.literal: Then he managed the Office of the Three Ranks, was promoted to Supervising Secretariat Drafter, and as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works and academician of the Hall for Assembling Worthies became prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then managed the Office of the Three Ranks, was promoted to Supervising Secretariat Drafter, and as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works and academician of the Hall for Assembling Worthies was appointed prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 不赴，改刑部侍郎致仕。

translations.literal: He did not take up the post; he was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He did not take up the post and was instead made Vice Minister of Justice and allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，進兵部，卒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong ascended, he was promoted in the Ministry of War rank and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong ascended, he was promoted in the Ministry of War rank and died.

sentences.zh: 本名皞，字子融。

translations.literal: His original name was Hao; his style name was Zirong.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Hao; his style name was Zirong.

sentences.zh: 元昊反，請以字為名。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao rebelled, he requested to use his style name as his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao rebelled, he requested to use his style name as his personal name.

sentences.zh: 性儉嗇，街道卒除道，侵子融邸店尺寸地，至自詣開封府訴之。

translations.literal: By nature he was frugal and stingy. When street sweeper soldiers cleared the road and encroached on Zirong's lodge property by inches, he personally went to Kaifeng prefectural office to lodge a complaint.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was frugal and stingy. When street sweeper soldiers clearing the road encroached on his lodge property by inches, he personally went to the Kaifeng prefectural office to lodge a complaint.

sentences.zh: 然教飭子孫，嚴厲有家法。

translations.literal: Yet he instructed and disciplined his descendants—strict, with established family rules.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he instructed and disciplined his descendants with strict family rules.

sentences.zh: 晚學佛氏，從僧懷璉遊。

translations.literal: In later years he studied Buddhist teachings and associated with the monk Huailian.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he studied Buddhism and associated with the monk Huailian.

sentences.zh: 張知白

translations.literal: Zhang Zhibai
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhibai

sentences.zh: 張知白，字用晦，滄州清池人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhibai, style name Yonghui, was a native of Qingchi in Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhibai, whose style name was Yonghui, was a native of Qingchi in Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼篤學，中進士第，累遷河陽節度判官。

translations.literal: From youth he studied devotedly, passed the jinshi examination, and was successively promoted to administrative aide of the Heyang military commission.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied devotedly, passed the jinshi examination, and rose to administrative aide of the Heyang military commission.

sentences.zh: 咸平中疏言當今要務，真宗異之，召試舍人院，權右正言。

translations.literal: During Xianping he submitted a memorial on pressing affairs of the day; Emperor Zhenzong was impressed, summoned him for examination at the Drafting Academy, and made him acting Right Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianping he submitted a memorial on pressing affairs of the day; Emperor Zhenzong was impressed, summoned him for examination at the Drafting Academy, and made him acting Right Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 獻《鳳扆箴》，出知劍州。

translations.literal: He presented Admonition at the Phoenix Screen and was sent out as prefect of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He presented Admonition at the Phoenix Screen and was sent out as prefect of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 逾年，召試中書，加直史館，面賜五品服，判三司開拆司。

translations.literal: After a year he was summoned for examination at the Secretariat, given concurrent appointment to the Historiography Institute, personally granted fifth-rank robes, and made administrator of the Three Bureaus Opening and Review Office.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was summoned for examination at the Secretariat, given concurrent appointment to the Historiography Institute, personally granted fifth-rank robes, and made administrator of the Three Bureaus Opening and Review Office.

sentences.zh: 江南旱，與李防分路安撫。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan suffered drought, he and Li Fang were sent by separate routes as pacification commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangnan suffered drought, he and Li Fang were sent by separate routes as pacification commissioners.

sentences.zh: 及還，權管勾京東轉運使事。

translations.literal: Upon return he temporarily managed the affairs of the eastern capital transport commission.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his return he temporarily managed the affairs of the eastern capital transport commission.

sentences.zh: 周伯星見，司天以瑞奏，群臣伏閣稱賀。

translations.literal: The star Zhoubo appeared; the Astronomy Office reported it as an auspicious sign and the officials prostrated themselves at the gate to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The star Zhoubo appeared; the Astronomy Office reported it as an auspicious sign, and officials prostrated themselves at the gate to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 知白以為人君當修德應天，而星之見伏無所繫，因陳治道之要。

translations.literal: Zhibai held that a ruler should cultivate virtue in response to Heaven, while the appearing and hiding of stars had no bearing; he therefore set forth the essentials of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhibai held that a ruler should cultivate virtue in response to Heaven, while the appearance and disappearance of stars had no bearing; he therefore set forth the essentials of good governance.

sentences.zh: 帝謂宰臣曰：「知白可謂乃心朝廷矣。

translations.literal: The emperor told the chief ministers, "Zhibai can be said to devote his heart to the court."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the chief ministers, "Zhibai can truly be said to devote his heart to the court."

sentences.zh: 」東封，進右司諫。

translations.literal: During the eastern Fengshan rites he was promoted to Right Remonstrance Official of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the eastern Fengshan rites he was promoted to Right Remonstrance Official of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 又言：「咸平中，河湟未平，臣嘗請罷郡國所上祥瑞。

translations.literal: He further said, "During Xianping, when Hehuang was not yet pacified, I once requested cessation of auspicious portents submitted by commanderies and prefectures."
translations.idiomatic: He further said, "During Xianping, when Hehuang was not yet pacified, I once requested that commanderies and prefectures cease submitting reports of auspicious portents."

sentences.zh: 今天下無事，靈貺並至，望以《泰山諸瑞圖》寘玉清昭應宮，其副藏秘閣。」

translations.literal: Now all under Heaven is at peace and numinous blessings arrive together. I hope The Various Portents of Mount Tai may be placed in the Palace of Jade Purity and Resonance with Heaven, with a duplicate stored in the Secret Archive."
translations.idiomatic: Now all under Heaven is at peace and numinous blessings arrive together. I hope The Various Portents of Mount Tai may be placed in the Palace of Jade Purity and Resonance with Heaven, with a duplicate stored in the Secret Archive."

sentences.zh: 陝西饑，命按巡之。

translations.literal: Shaanxi suffered famine; he was ordered to inspect and tour there.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaanxi suffered famine, he was ordered to inspect and tour the region.

sentences.zh: 尋知鄧州。

translations.literal: Soon he became prefect of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he became prefect of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 會關右流傭至境，知白既發倉廩，又募民出粟以濟。

translations.literal: When migrant laborers from the west reached his border, Zhibai both opened granaries and solicited grain from the people to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: When migrant laborers from the west reached his jurisdiction, Zhibai opened granaries and solicited grain from the people to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 擢龍圖閣待制、知審官院，再遷尚書工部郎中，使契丹。

translations.literal: He was elevated to Attendant Drafting in the Dragon Diagram Hall and director of the Office of Merit Evaluation; again promoted to Langzhong in the Ministry of Works and sent as envoy to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: He was elevated to Attendant Drafting in the Dragon Diagram Hall and director of the Office of Merit Evaluation, then promoted to Langzhong in the Ministry of Works and sent as envoy to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 知白以朝廷制官，重內輕外，為引唐李嶠議遷臺閣典藩郡，乃自請補外，不許，遂命糾察在京刑獄，固請，知青州。

translations.literal: Zhibai held that the court valued inner posts and slighted outer ones; citing Tang Li Jiao's proposal to transfer palace officials to frontier prefectures, he himself requested an outer appointment. This was not granted; he was then ordered to inspect capital criminal cases, but he firmly requested and was made prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhibai held that the court valued inner posts and slighted outer ones; citing Tang Li Jiao's proposal to transfer palace officials to frontier prefectures, he requested an outer appointment himself. When this was denied, he was ordered to inspect capital criminal cases, but he firmly pressed his request and was made prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 還京師，求領國子監。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he requested to head the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the capital, he requested to head the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「知白豈倦於處劇邪？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Is Zhibai weary of handling difficult duties?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Is Zhibai weary of handling difficult duties?"

sentences.zh: 」宰臣言：「知白更踐中外，未嘗為身謀。

translations.literal: The chief ministers said, "Zhibai has served both at court and in the provinces and has never schemed for himself."
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers said, "Zhibai has served both at court and in the provinces and has never schemed for himself."

sentences.zh: 」乃遷右諫議大夫、權御史中丞、拜給事中、參知政事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was transferred to Right Remonstrance Grandee, acting Vice Censor-in-Chief, appointed Supervising Secretariat Drafter and Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was transferred to Right Remonstrance Grandee and acting Vice Censor-in-Chief, appointed Supervising Secretariat Drafter and Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 知白在相位，慎名器，無毫髪私。

translations.literal: While Zhibai held the chancellorship, he was careful with titles and appointments and showed not a hair's breadth of private interest.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as chancellor, Zhibai was scrupulous in conferring titles and showed not the slightest private favoritism.

sentences.zh: 常以盛滿為戒，雖顯貴，其清約如寒士。

translations.literal: He often took fullness and excess as warning; though eminent and honored, his frugality and restraint were like those of a poor scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He often warned himself against the dangers of peak success; though eminent and honored, he lived as frugally as a poor scholar.

sentences.zh: 然體素羸，憂畏日侵，在中書忽感風眩，輿歸第。

translations.literal: Yet his constitution had always been weak; worry and fear daily encroached. At the Secretariat he suddenly suffered dizziness from wind and was borne by carriage back to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had always been frail in constitution, and worry and fear wore on him daily. While at the Secretariat he was suddenly struck with vertigo and was carried home by carriage.

sentences.zh: 帝親問疾，不能語，薨。

translations.literal: The emperor personally inquired after his illness; he could not speak and died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally inquired after his illness, but he could no longer speak and soon died.

sentences.zh: 為罷上巳宴，贈太傅、中書令。

translations.literal: For his sake the Third Day of the Third Month banquet was canceled; he was posthumously given Grand Tutor and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The court canceled the Third Day of the Third Month banquet in his honor and posthumously granted him the titles of Grand Tutor and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 禮官謝絳議諡「文節」，御史王嘉言：「知白守道徇公，當官不撓，可謂正矣，諡『文正』。

translations.literal: Ritual official Xie Jiang proposed the posthumous title "Cultured Restraint"; Censor Wang Jiayan said, "Zhibai upheld the Way and served the public, and in office would not be bent—this may be called upright; let the title be 'Cultured Uprightness.'"
translations.idiomatic: Ritual official Xie Jiang proposed the posthumous title "Cultured Restraint," but Censor Wang Jiayan argued, "Zhibai upheld the Way, served the public, and would not yield in office—he was truly upright. The title should be 'Cultured Uprightness.'"

sentences.zh: 」王曾曰：「『文節』，美諡矣。

translations.literal: Wang Ceng said, "'Cultured Restraint' is already a fine posthumous title."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ceng said, "'Cultured Restraint' is already a fine posthumous title."

sentences.zh: 」遂不改。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: The title was therefore left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 知白九歲，其父終邢州，殯於佛寺。

translations.literal: When Zhibai was nine, his father died in Xingzhou and the body was temporarily interred at a Buddhist temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhibai was nine, his father died in Xingzhou and was temporarily interred in a Buddhist temple.

sentences.zh: 及契丹寇河北，寺宇多頹廢，殯不可辨。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded Hebei, many temple buildings fell into ruin and the temporary burial could no longer be identified.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded Hebei, many temples fell into ruin and the temporary burial could no longer be identified.

sentences.zh: 知白既登第，徒行訪之，得佛寺殿基，恍然識其處。

translations.literal: After Zhibai passed the examination, he went on foot to search for it, found the foundation of the temple hall, and suddenly recognized the place.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the examination, Zhibai went on foot to search for the spot, found the foundation of the temple hall, and suddenly recognized the place.

sentences.zh: 既發，其衣衾皆可驗，眾歎其誠孝。

translations.literal: Once it was exhumed, the clothing and shroud could all be verified, and all admired his sincere filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When the grave was opened, the clothing and shroud were all intact, and all marveled at his sincere filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 嘗過陝州，與通判孫何遇，讀道旁古碑凡數千言，及還，知白略無所遺。

translations.literal: Once passing through Shaanzhou he met Vice Prefect Sun He, read an ancient stele by the roadside of several thousand characters, and upon return Zhibai recalled nearly nothing missing.
translations.idiomatic: Once while passing through Shaanzhou he met Vice Prefect Sun He and read an ancient stele by the roadside of several thousand characters; when tested afterward, Zhibai recalled nearly every word.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，契丹大閱，聲言獵幽州，朝廷患之。

translations.literal: During Tiansheng the Khitan held a great review and publicly announced they would hunt in Youzhou; the court was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiansheng era, the Khitan held a grand military review and announced they would hunt in Youzhou; the court was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 帝以問二府，眾曰：「備粟練師，以備不虞。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the two executive bureaus; many said, "Stock grain and drill troops to guard against the unforeseen."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted the executive bureaus; many officials said, "Stock grain and drill troops to guard against the unforeseen."

sentences.zh: 」知白曰：「不然，契丹修好未遠，今其舉者，以上初政，試觀朝廷耳，豈可自生釁邪！

translations.literal: Zhibai said, "Not so. The Khitan made peace not long ago; their present move is simply to test the court at the start of a new reign—not grounds to provoke conflict ourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhibai said, "No. The Khitan made peace with us not long ago. This move is merely to test the court at the beginning of a new reign—why should we provoke conflict ourselves?"

sentences.zh: 若終以為疑，莫如因今河決，發兵以防河為名，彼亦不虞也。

translations.literal: If they still harbor suspicion, best to take advantage of the present river breach and mobilize troops in the name of flood control—the Khitan will suspect nothing.
translations.idiomatic: If the court remains uneasy, we could take advantage of the current river breach and mobilize troops under the pretext of flood control—they would suspect nothing.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，契丹果罷去。

translations.literal: Before long the Khitan indeed withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Khitan indeed withdrew.

sentences.zh: 無子，以兄子子思為後，仕至尚書工部侍郎致仕。

translations.literal: He had no sons and made his elder brother's son Zisi his heir; Zisi served up to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Having no sons, he adopted his elder brother's son Zisi as his heir. Zisi rose to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works and retired.

sentences.zh: 杜衍，字世昌，越州山陰人。

translations.literal: Du Yan, style name Shichang, was a native of Shanyin in Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan, whose style name was Shichang, was a native of Shanyin in Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 父遂良，仕至尚書度支員外郎。

translations.literal: His father Suiliang served up to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue's Expenditure Section.
translations.idiomatic: His father Suiliang had served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue's Expenditure Section.

sentences.zh: 衍總髪苦志厲操，尤篤於學。

translations.literal: From childhood Yan set his mind on hardship and steeling his conduct, and was especially devoted to learning.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Yan dedicated himself to rigorous discipline and was especially devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 擢進士甲科，補揚州觀察推官，改秘書省著作佐郎、知平遙縣。

translations.literal: He was selected in the top tier of the jinshi examination, appointed investigative official of Yangzhou observation commission, then changed to Assistant Compiler in the Secretariat and prefect of Pingyao County.
translations.idiomatic: Selected in the top tier of the jinshi examination, he was appointed investigative official for Yangzhou, then transferred to Assistant Compiler in the Secretariat and appointed prefect of Pingyao County.

sentences.zh: 使者薦之，通判晉州。

translations.literal: An envoy recommended him and he became vice prefect of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial envoy recommended him, and he was made vice prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔舉良吏，擢知乾州。

translations.literal: An edict called for worthy administrators; he was promoted to prefect of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict called for worthy administrators, he was promoted to prefect of Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 陳堯諮安撫陝西，有詔藩府乃賜宴，堯諮至乾州，以衍賢，特賜宴，仍徙衍權知鳳翔府。

translations.literal: When Chen Yaozi pacified Shaanxi, there was an edict that feudatory prefectures alone received banquets. When Yaozi reached Qianzhou, deeming Yan worthy, he specially granted a banquet and transferred Yan to acting prefect of Fengxiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Yaozi was pacification commissioner for Shaanxi, an edict provided banquets only for feudatory prefectures. When Yaozi reached Qianzhou, he deemed Yan worthy of special honor and granted him a banquet, then transferred him to acting prefect of Fengxiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及罷歸，二州民邀留境上，曰：「何奪我賢太守也？

translations.literal: When he finished and returned, the people of both prefectures intercepted him at the border, saying, "Why take away our worthy prefect?"
translations.idiomatic: When he completed his tour and departed, the people of both prefectures intercepted him at the border, crying, "Why take away our worthy prefect?"

sentences.zh: 」以太常博士提點河東路刑獄，遷尚書祠部員外郎。

translations.literal: As Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices he was inspector of criminal cases on the Hedong circuit, then promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites' Ancestral Temples Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed inspector of criminal cases on the Hedong circuit as Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites' Ancestral Temples Section.

sentences.zh: 按行潞州，折冤獄，知州王曙為作《辨獄記》。

translations.literal: Touring Luzhou he redressed unjust cases; Prefect Wang Shu wrote A Record of Judging Prison Cases about it.
translations.idiomatic: While touring Luzhou he redressed unjust cases, and Prefect Wang Shu wrote A Record of Judging Prison Cases in commemoration.

sentences.zh: 高繼昇知石州，人告繼昇連蕃族謀變，逮捕繫治，久不決，衍辯其誣，抵告者罪。

translations.literal: Gao Jisheng governed Shizhou; someone reported that Jisheng colluded with frontier tribes to rebel. He was arrested and detained for long without verdict; Yan proved the charge false and punished the accuser.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jisheng was prefect of Shizhou when someone accused him of colluding with frontier tribes to rebel. Jisheng was arrested and detained without verdict for a long time until Yan proved the charge false and punished the accuser.

sentences.zh: 寧化軍守將鞫人死罪，不以實，衍覆正之。

translations.literal: A garrison commander of Ninghua Army tried a capital case without establishing facts; Yan reviewed and corrected it.
translations.idiomatic: A garrison commander of Ninghua Army tried a capital case without establishing the facts; Yan reviewed the case and corrected the judgment.

sentences.zh: 守將不伏，訴之，詔為置獄，果不當死。

translations.literal: The commander would not submit and appealed; an edict ordered a new trial, and indeed the penalty of death was inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The commander refused to accept the ruling and appealed; the emperor ordered a retrial, which confirmed that the death penalty was unwarranted.

sentences.zh: 徒京西路，又徙知揚州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the western capital circuit, then again made prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the western capital circuit and later appointed prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 有司奏衍辨獄法當賞，遷刑部。

translations.literal: The relevant office memorialized that Yan's judging of cases merited reward; he was promoted in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office memorialized that Yan deserved reward for his judicial work, and he was promoted in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 章獻太后遣使安撫淮南，使還，未及他語，問杜衍安否，使者以治狀對。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Zhangxian sent envoys to pacify Huainan; when they returned, before other talk she asked whether Du Yan was well, and the envoys answered with reports of his governance.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Zhangxian sent envoys to pacify Huainan. When they returned, before speaking of anything else she asked whether Du Yan was well; the envoys answered with reports of his governance.

sentences.zh: 太后歎曰：「吾知之久矣。」

translations.literal: The empress dowager sighed and said, "I have known of him for long."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager sighed and said, "I have known of him for a long time."

sentences.zh: 徙河東轉運副使、陝西轉運使。

translations.literal: Transferred to deputy transport commissioner of Hedong and transport commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to deputy transport commissioner of Hedong and transport commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 召為三司戶部副使，擢天章閣待制、知江陵府。

translations.literal: Summoned as Deputy Commissioner of the Households Bureau of the Three Bureaus; promoted to Attendant Drafting in the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and prefect of Jiangling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Deputy Commissioner of the Households Bureau of the Three Bureaus, then promoted to Attendant Drafting in the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and appointed prefect of Jiangling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未行，會河北乏軍費，選為都轉運使，遷工部郎中，不增賦於民而用足。

translations.literal: Before he departed, when Hebei lacked military funds he was selected as metropolitan transport commissioner, promoted to Langzhong in the Ministry of Works, and without increasing levies on the people the funds were sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, Hebei ran short of military funds and he was selected as metropolitan transport commissioner. Promoted to Langzhong in the Ministry of Works, he supplied the needed funds without increasing levies on the people.

sentences.zh: 還為樞密直學士。

translations.literal: Returning, he became Academician on Direct Staff of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he became Academician on Direct Staff of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 求補外，以右諫議大夫知天雄軍。

translations.literal: He requested an outer appointment and was made Right Remonstrance Grandee and prefect of Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: He requested an appointment outside the capital and was made Right Remonstrance Grandee and prefect of Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 始，衍為治謹密，不以威刑督吏，然吏民亦憚其清整。

translations.literal: At first Yan governed with meticulous care, not relying on harsh punishments to supervise officials, yet officials and people alike feared his upright austerity.
translations.idiomatic: Yan governed with meticulous care and did not rely on harsh punishments to drive his officials, yet officials and commoners alike stood in awe of his upright austerity.

sentences.zh: 仁宗特召為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong specially summoned him as Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong specially summoned him to serve as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「中書、樞密，古之三事大臣，所謂坐而論道者也。

translations.literal: He memorialized, "The Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs were the Three Great Ministers of antiquity, those who 'sat and deliberated upon the Way.'"
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "The Secretariat and the Bureau of Military Affairs correspond to the Three Great Ministers of antiquity—the ministers who 'sit and deliberate upon the Way.'"

sentences.zh: 止隻日對前殿，何以盡天下之事？

translations.literal: Meeting only on alternate days in the front hall—how can they exhaust the affairs of all under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Meeting the emperor only on alternate days in the front hall—how can they exhaust the affairs of the realm?

sentences.zh: 宜迭召見，賜坐便殿，以極獻替可否，其他，不必親煩陛下也。

translations.literal: They should be summoned in rotation and granted seats in the side hall to fully present and withdraw proposals; other matters need not personally trouble Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: They should be summoned in rotation and granted seats in the side hall so they might fully debate what should be adopted or rejected; other matters need not personally burden Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」又議常平法曰：「歲有豐凶，穀有貴賤，官以法平之，則農有餘利矣。

translations.literal: He also discussed the Ever-Normal Granary law: "Years have plenty and shortage, grain has high and low prices; when the state levels them by law, farmers will have surplus profit."
translations.idiomatic: He also addressed the Ever-Normal Granary system: "Years have plenty and want, grain has high prices and low; when the state levels prices by law, farmers will enjoy surplus profit."

sentences.zh: 今豪商大賈，乘時賤收，水旱，則稽伏而不出，冀其翔踴，以圖厚利，而困吾民也。

translations.literal: Now great merchants and traders buy cheap at opportune times; in flood and drought they hoard and refuse to release, hoping prices soar for thick profit, thereby distressing our people.
translations.idiomatic: Now great merchants buy cheap when prices fall; in flood or drought they hoard grain and refuse to sell, hoping prices will soar so they may reap thick profits—thereby distressing our people.

sentences.zh: 請量州郡遠近，戶口眾寡，嚴賞罰，課責官吏，出納無壅，增損有宜。

translations.literal: I request measuring distance of prefectures and commanderies, size of households and population, enforcing strict rewards and punishments, charging officials with responsibility, allowing no obstruction in intake and outflow, and making increases and decreases appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the distances of prefectures, the size of their populations, strict rewards and punishments, and the accountability of officials be calibrated so that grain may flow without obstruction and purchases and releases may be properly gauged.

sentences.zh: 公糴未充，則禁爭糴以規利者；

translations.literal: When public purchases are not yet full, ban those who compete to buy grain for profit;
translations.idiomatic: When public stores are not yet full, those who compete to buy grain for profit should be banned;

sentences.zh: 糴畢而儲之，則察其以供軍為名而假借者。

translations.literal: When purchases are complete and stored, investigate those who under the pretext of supplying the army engage in borrowing and misuse.
translations.idiomatic: once purchases are complete and grain is stored, investigate those who misappropriate stores under the pretext of military supply.

sentences.zh: 州郡闕母錢，願出官帑助之。

translations.literal: Where prefectures and commanderies lack seed capital, I wish to lend from state treasuries to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: Where prefectures lack seed capital, I ask that the state treasury provide assistance.

sentences.zh: 否則勸課之官，家至日見，亦奚益於事哉。」

translations.literal: Otherwise the encouragement-and-supervision officials may visit every household daily—yet how does that benefit the matter?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise officials sent to encourage compliance may visit every household daily—and what good will that do?

sentences.zh: 兼判吏部流內銓。

translations.literal: Concurrently judged the Ministry of Personnel's Flowing Within Selection Office.
translations.idiomatic: He concurrently administered the Ministry of Personnel's Flowing Within Selection Office.

sentences.zh: 選補科格繁長，主判不能悉閱，吏多受賕，出縮為奸。

translations.literal: Selection and appointment regulations were numerous and long; the chief judge could not review all; clerks often took bribes and shortened or reduced qualifications to commit fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Selection regulations were voluminous; the chief judge could not review them all, and clerks often took bribes and manipulated qualifications to commit fraud.

sentences.zh: 衍既視事，即敕吏函銓法，問曰：「盡乎？

translations.literal: Once Yan assumed duties, he immediately ordered clerks to box the selection laws and asked, "Are these complete?"
translations.idiomatic: Once Yan assumed office, he ordered the clerks to assemble the selection regulations in a box and asked, "Is this everything?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「盡矣。

translations.literal: They said, "All are here."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "This is everything."

sentences.zh: 」力閱視，具得本末曲折。

translations.literal: He personally reviewed them with force and fully grasped every turn and detail from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: He reviewed them himself with painstaking care until he grasped every detail from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 明日，令諸吏無得升堂，各坐曹聽行文書，銓事悉自予奪，由是吏不能為奸利。

translations.literal: The next day he ordered all clerks not to ascend the hall; each sat in his bureau to receive and dispatch documents; all selection matters were decided by himself alone—whereupon clerks could no longer commit fraud for profit.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he barred clerks from the main hall; each remained at his desk to receive and dispatch documents while Yan personally decided every selection matter—whereupon the clerks could no longer profit by fraud.

sentences.zh: 數月，聲動京師。

translations.literal: Within several months his reputation shook the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Within months his reputation resounded throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 改知審官院，其裁制如判銓時。

translations.literal: Transferred to director of the Office of Merit Evaluation; his restraining governance was as when he judged selection.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the Office of Merit Evaluation and governed it with the same firm hand he had shown at Selection.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書工部侍郎、知永興軍。

translations.literal: Promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works and prefect of Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works and appointed prefect of Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 民有晝亡其婦者，為設方略捕，立得殺人賊，發所瘞屍，並得賊殺他婦人屍二，秦人大驚。

translations.literal: A man whose wife vanished by day—Yan devised stratagems to capture the culprit, immediately obtained the murderer, exhumed the buried corpse, and also recovered two other women's corpses the thief had killed; the people of Qin were greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: When a man reported that his wife had vanished in broad daylight, Yan devised a plan to capture the killer, quickly seized the murderer, exhumed the buried corpse, and recovered two other women's corpses the killer had buried as well; the people of the region were astonished.

sentences.zh: 徙并州。

translations.literal: Transferred to Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 元昊反，以太原要衝，加龍圖閣學士。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao rebelled, because Taiyuan was a strategic pass he was given the additional title of Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao rebelled, Taiyuan being a strategic pass, Yan was given the additional title of Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 寶元二年，遷刑部侍郎、復知永興軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoyuan he was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice and again made prefect of Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoyuan he was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice and again appointed prefect of Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 時方用兵，民苦調發，吏因緣為奸。

translations.literal: At the time warfare was underway; the people suffered from requisition and dispatch; officials took opportunity for fraud.
translations.idiomatic: War was then underway; the people suffered under requisition and dispatch, and officials seized the opportunity for fraud.

sentences.zh: 衍區處計畫，量道里遠近，寬其期會，使民得次第輸官，比他州費，省錢過半。

translations.literal: Yan arranged and planned, measuring distance of routes and extending deadlines, enabling the people to deliver to the government in sequence; compared with other prefectures the expenses were reduced by more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Yan devised a plan calibrated to distances and routes, extended deadlines, and enabled the people to deliver levies in orderly sequence—cutting costs by more than half compared with other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 召還，權知開封府，權近聞衍名，莫敢干以私。

translations.literal: Summoned back to acting prefect of Kaifeng Prefecture; those in power had heard Yan's name and none dared approach him with private requests.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to serve as acting prefect of Kaifeng, those in power had heard of Yan's reputation and none dared approach him with private requests.

sentences.zh: 拜同知樞密院事，改樞密副使。

translations.literal: Appointed Co-Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; changed to Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Co-Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then made Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 夏竦上攻守策，宰相欲用出師。

translations.literal: Xia Song submitted attack-and-defense stratagems; the chancellor wished to deploy troops in campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Song submitted stratagems for attack and defense, and the chancellor wished to launch a military campaign.

sentences.zh: 衍曰：「僥倖成功，非萬全計。

translations.literal: Yan said, "Seeking success by chance is not a plan of complete security."
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "Gambling on success is not a fully reliable plan."

sentences.zh: 」爭議久之，求罷不許，賜手詔敦勉。

translations.literal: They disputed long; he requested dismissal and was not permitted; the emperor personally wrote an edict earnestly encouraging him.
translations.idiomatic: They debated at length; Yan requested to be relieved but was refused, and the emperor sent a personal edict earnestly urging him to remain.

sentences.zh: 為河東宣撫使，拜吏部侍郎、樞密使。

translations.literal: Made pacification commissioner of Hedong; appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made pacification commissioner of Hedong and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 每內降恩，率寢格不行，積詔旨至十數，輒納帝前。

translations.literal: Whenever imperial grace came by inner edict, he usually shelved the regulations and did not implement them; when edicts accumulated to ten or more, he would return them before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever imperial favors arrived by private edict, he usually held the regulations in abeyance and refused to implement them; when such edicts accumulated to a dozen or more, he would return them to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 諫官歐陽修入對，帝曰：「外人知杜衍封還內降邪？

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Ouyang Xiu entered audience; the emperor said, "Do outsiders know that Du Yan returns private edicts sealed?"
translations.idiomatic: When Remonstrance official Ouyang Xiu entered audience, the emperor said, "Do outsiders know that Du Yan returns private edicts unopened?"

sentences.zh: 凡有求於朕，每以衍不可告之而止者，多於所封還也。」

translations.literal: "All who seek from me, each time stop because they say Yan cannot be told—are more numerous than those returned sealed."
translations.idiomatic: "Those who seek favors of me and stop because they say Yan cannot be told are even more numerous than those whose edicts he returns sealed."

sentences.zh: 契丹與元昊戰黃河外，參知政事范仲淹宣撫河東，欲以兵自從。

translations.literal: The Khitan fought Yuan Hao outside the Yellow River; Vice Grand Councillor Fan Zhongyan pacified Hedong and wished to take troops with him.
