translations.idiomatic: While the Khitan fought Yuan Hao beyond the Yellow River, Vice Grand Councillor Fan Zhongyan was pacification commissioner for Hedong and wished to take troops with him.

sentences.zh: 衍曰：「二國方交鬥，勢必不來，我兵不可妄出。

translations.literal: Yan said, "The two states are presently fighting each other—they will certainly not come here; our troops must not be rashly deployed."
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "The two states are fighting each other—they will certainly not threaten us. Our troops must not be rashly deployed."

sentences.zh: 」仲淹爭議帝前，詆衍，語甚切。

translations.literal: Zhongyan disputed before the emperor, denounced Yan, and his words were very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan debated before the emperor, denounced Yan, and spoke in harsh terms.

sentences.zh: 仲淹嘗父行事衍，衍不以為恨。

translations.literal: Zhongyan had treated Yan as a father in conduct; Yan did not take it as resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhongyan had once treated Yan with the deference due a father, Yan bore him no resentment.

sentences.zh: 契丹婿劉三嘏避罪來歸，輔臣議厚館之，以詰契丹陰事。

translations.literal: The Khitan son-in-law Liu Sanguo fled guilt and came to surrender; chief ministers debated generously hosting him to interrogate Khitan secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sanguo, son-in-law of the Khitan ruler, fled to avoid punishment; chief ministers debated granting him generous hospitality to extract intelligence on Khitan secrets.

sentences.zh: 諫官歐陽修亦請留三嘏，帝以問衍。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Ouyang Xiu also requested detaining Sanguo; the emperor asked Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Ouyang Xiu also asked that Sanguo be detained; the emperor consulted Yan.

sentences.zh: 衍曰：「中國主忠信，若自違誓約，納叛亡，則不直在我。

translations.literal: Yan said, "The Middle Kingdom upholds loyalty and trust; if we ourselves violate sworn treaties and harbor fugitive rebels, rightness will not be on our side."
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "Our realm upholds loyalty and trust. If we violate sworn treaties and harbor fugitive rebels, the moral right will not be with us."

sentences.zh: 且三嘏為契丹近親，而逋逃來歸，其謀身若此，尚足與謀國乎！

translations.literal: Moreover Sanguo is close kin of the Khitan, yet fleeing and coming over—if he plots for himself like this, is he fit to plot for the state!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Sanguo is close kin to the Khitan, yet he fled to us to save himself—if he schemed thus for his own survival, how could he be trusted in affairs of state?

sentences.zh: 納之何益，不如還之。

translations.literal: What profit in accepting him—better to return him.
translations.idiomatic: What good would accepting him do? Better to return him.

sentences.zh: 」乃還三嘏。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sanguo was returned.
translations.idiomatic: Sanguo was therefore returned.

sentences.zh: 拜同平章事、集賢殿大學士兼樞密使。

translations.literal: Appointed Grand Councillor, Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling Worthies, and concurrently Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Councillor, Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling Worthies, and concurrently Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 衍好薦引賢士，而沮止僥倖，小人多不悅。

translations.literal: Yan loved recommending worthy men and obstructing those who sought luck; petty men were often displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yan loved to recommend worthy men and obstruct opportunists; petty men were often displeased with him.

sentences.zh: 其婿蘇舜欽，少年能文章，論議稍侵權貴，監進奏院，循前例，祠神以伎樂娛賓，集賢校理王益柔為衍所知，或言益柔嘗戲作《傲歌》，御史皆劾奏之，欲因以危衍。

translations.literal: His son-in-law Su Shunchin, young and able in literary composition, in debate somewhat encroached on powerful families; as overseer of the Memorial Submission Office he followed precedent in using music and entertainment to feast guests at a temple sacrifice; Wang Yirou, collator of the Hall for Assembling Worthies and known to Yan, someone reported Yirou had playfully composed A Song of Arrogance; the censors all impeached and memorialized, wishing thereby to endanger Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His son-in-law Su Shunchin, a young man skilled in writing whose opinions sometimes affronted powerful families, oversaw the Memorial Submission Office and, following precedent, entertained guests with music at a temple sacrifice. Wang Yirou, a collator in the Hall for Assembling Worthies whom Yan knew, was reported to have mockingly composed A Song of Arrogance. The censors all impeached the matter, hoping thereby to imperil Yan.

sentences.zh: 諫官孫甫言：「丁度因對求大用，請屬吏。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Sun Fu said, "Ding Du on audience sought great appointment and asked to assign subordinate officials."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Sun Fu reported, "Ding Du sought a major appointment in audience and asked to assign subordinate officials."

sentences.zh: 」度知甫所奏誤，力求置對。

translations.literal: Du, knowing what Fu memorialized was wrong, urgently requested a face-to-face audience to rebut.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Du, knowing Fu's report was mistaken, urgently requested a face-to-face audience to rebut it.

sentences.zh: 衍以甫方奉使契丹，寢甫奏，度深銜之。

translations.literal: Yan, because Fu was then on mission to the Khitan, shelved Fu's memorial; Du deeply harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fu was then on mission to the Khitan, Yan shelved his memorial; Ding Du deeply resented this.

sentences.zh: 及衍罷，度草制指衍朋比。

translations.literal: When Yan was dismissed, Du drafted the appointment edict pointing to Yan's factional collusion.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was dismissed, Ding Du drafted the appointment edict accusing Yan of factional collusion.

sentences.zh: 時范仲淹、富弼欲更理天下事，與用事者不合，仲淹、弼既出宣撫，言者附會，益攻二人之短。

translations.literal: At the time Fan Zhongyan and Fu Bi wished to reorder affairs of all under Heaven and clashed with those in power; once Zhongyan and Bi went out as pacification commissioners, critics attached themselves and increasingly attacked the two men's faults.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Fan Zhongyan and Fu Bi sought to reform the governance of the realm and clashed with those in power. Once Zhongyan and Bi went out as pacification commissioners, critics seized the moment and increasingly attacked their faults.

sentences.zh: 帝欲罷仲淹、弼政事，衍獨左右之，然衍平日議論，實非朋比也。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to remove Zhongyan and Bi from office; Yan alone supported them, yet Yan's daily discourse truly was not factional collusion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to remove Zhongyan and Bi from office; Yan alone supported them, though in truth Yan's daily conduct was not factional collusion.

sentences.zh: 以尚書左丞出知兗州。

translations.literal: As Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs he was sent out as prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 慶曆七年，衍甫七十，上表請還印綬，乃以太子少師致仕。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qingli Yan had just turned seventy; he submitted a memorial requesting return of seal and sash, and was granted retirement as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Qingli, Yan having just turned seventy, he submitted a memorial requesting return of seal and sash and was granted retirement as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 衍為宰相，賈昌朝不喜，議者謂故相一上章得請，以三少致仕，皆非故事，蓋昌朝抑之也。

translations.literal: When Yan was chancellor, Jia Changchao disliked him; commentators said that a former chancellor obtaining request with one memorial, retiring as one of the Three Preceptors—all were without precedent, likely because Changchao suppressed him.
translations.idiomatic: While Yan served as chancellor, Jia Changchao disliked him. Commentators held that a former chancellor obtaining leave with a single memorial and retiring as one of the Three Preceptors were all without precedent—likely because Changchao had suppressed him.

sentences.zh: 皇祐元年，特遷太子太保，召陪祀明堂，仍詔應天府敦遣就道，都亭驛設帳具几杖待之，稱疾固辭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangyou he was specially promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, summoned to accompany sacrifice at the Bright Hall; still an edict ordered Yingtian Prefecture earnestly to escort him on the road, the Capital Pavilion Station set up tent and furnished couch and staff to await him—he pleaded illness and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangyou he was specially promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and summoned to accompany the Bright Hall sacrifice. An edict ordered Yingtian Prefecture to escort him posthaste; the Capital Pavilion Station prepared a tent with couch and staff to receive him—but he pleaded illness and firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 進太子太傅，賜其子同進士出身，又進太子太師。

translations.literal: Promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; his son was granted jinshi status; again promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; his son was granted the status of a successful jinshi candidate; he was then promoted again to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 知制誥王洙謁告歸應天府，有詔撫問，封祁國公。

translations.literal: Edict-drafter Wang Zhu requested leave to return to Yingtian Prefecture; there was an edict to comfort and inquire; enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Edict-drafter Wang Zhu requested leave to return to Yingtian Prefecture; the emperor sent an edict of inquiry and comfort and enfeoffed Yan as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 衍清介不殖私產，既退，寓南都凡十年，第室卑陋，才數十楹，居之裕如也。

translations.literal: Yan was upright and uncompromising and did not accumulate private property; after retirement he lodged in the southern capital for ten years in all; his residence was humble and cramped, only several dozen bays, yet he lived in it with ease.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and uncompromising, Yan accumulated no private wealth. After retirement he lived in the southern capital for ten years in a humble dwelling of only a few dozen bays, yet he was content.

sentences.zh: 出入從者十許人，烏帽、皂綈袍、革帶。

translations.literal: Going out and returning he had about ten followers; black cap, black silk robe, leather belt.
translations.idiomatic: When he went out he was attended by about ten followers, dressed in black cap, black silk robe, and leather belt.

sentences.zh: 或勸衍為居士服，衍曰：「老而謝事，尚可竊高士名邪！

translations.literal: Some urged Yan to wear lay Buddhist dress; Yan said, "Old and retired from office—can I still steal the name of lofty recluse!"
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to wear the garb of a lay Buddhist; Yan said, "Old and retired from office—can I still steal the name of a lofty recluse?"

sentences.zh: 」善為詩，正書、行、草皆有法、病革，帝遣中使賜藥，挾太醫往視，不及，卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He was skilled in composing poetry; in regular script, running script, and cursive script all had method. When gravely ill, the emperor sent palace envoys to bestow medicine and dispatched the imperial physician to examine him—too late; he died at age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at poetry, and his regular, running, and cursive scripts all had mastery. When gravely ill, the emperor sent palace envoys with medicine and an imperial physician—but they arrived too late. He died at eighty.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒兼侍中，諡「正獻」。

translations.literal: Posthumously given Grand Master and concurrent Palace Attendant; posthumous title "Upright Contribution."
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master and Concurrent Palace Attendant, with the posthumous title "Upright Contribution."

sentences.zh: 戒其子努力忠孝，斂以一枕一席，小壙庳塚以葬。

translations.literal: He admonished his sons to strive in loyalty and filial piety; burial with one pillow and one mat, a small vault and low mound.
translations.idiomatic: He admonished his sons to strive in loyalty and filial piety and was buried with a single pillow and mat in a small, low grave.

sentences.zh: 自作遺疏，其略曰：「無以久安而忽邊防，無以既富而輕財用，宜早建儲副，以安人心。

translations.literal: He himself composed a death memorial, its gist saying: "Do not because of long peace neglect frontier defense; do not because of existing wealth treat finances lightly; the heir designate should be established early to settle people's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: He composed his own death memorial, which in essence read: "Do not because of long peace neglect frontier defense; do not because of wealth treat finances lightly; establish the heir designate early to settle the people's hearts."

sentences.zh: 」語不及私。

translations.literal: His words did not touch on private matters.
translations.idiomatic: His words touched on no private matters.

sentences.zh: 論曰：李迪、王曾、張知白、杜衍，皆賢相也。

translations.literal: Commentary states: Li Di, Wang Ceng, Zhang Zhibai, and Du Yan—all were worthy chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Li Di, Wang Ceng, Zhang Zhibai, and Du Yan were all worthy chancellors.

sentences.zh: 四人風烈，往往相似。

translations.literal: The four men's character and stature were often similar.
translations.idiomatic: The moral stature of the four was often much alike.

sentences.zh: 方仁宗初立，章獻臨朝，頗挾其才，將有專制之患。

translations.literal: When Renzong had just ascended, Zhangxian held court, somewhat wielding her talent—there would be the peril of autocratic rule.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong first ascended, Empress Zhangxian held court and somewhat wielded her power; autocratic rule seemed imminent.

sentences.zh: 迪、曾正色危言，能使宦官近習，不敢窺覦；

translations.literal: Di and Ceng with stern countenance spoke alarming words, able to make eunuchs and close attendants not dare to covet.
translations.idiomatic: Di and Ceng spoke with stern countenance and dire warning, so that eunuchs and close attendants did not dare to covet power;

sentences.zh: 而仁宗君德日就，章獻亦全令名，古人所謂社稷臣，於斯見之。

translations.literal: And Emperor Renzong's sovereign virtue daily matured; Zhangxian also preserved a good name—the so-called "ministers of state and altars" of antiquity are seen in this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong's virtue ripened day by day, and Empress Zhangxian preserved her good name—in them one sees what the ancients called ministers of the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 知白、衍勁正清約，皆能靳惜名器，裁抑僥幸，凜然有大臣之概焉。

translations.literal: Zhibai and Yan were firm, upright, and frugal—all able to cherish titles and restrain those who sought luck, imposing as great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhibai and Yan were firm, upright, and frugal; both cherished official titles and checked opportunists—bearing the true bearing of great ministers.

sentences.zh: 宋之賢相，莫盛於真、仁之世，漢魏相，唐宋璟、楊綰，豈得專美哉！

translations.literal: Among Song's worthy chancellors, none flourished more than in the Zhenzong and Renzong reigns—Han and Wei's chancellors, Tang's Song Jing and Yang Wan—how could they alone monopolize praise!
translations.idiomatic: Among the worthy chancellors of Song, none were more numerous than in the reigns of Emperors Zhenzong and Renzong—so how could the chancellors of Han and Wei, or Tang's Song Jing and Yang Wan, alone claim the glory?
